lines.text: Enter Leonato, Hero, Beatrice and others, with a Messenger.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I learn in this letter that Don Pedro of Arragon comes this night

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: to Messina.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He is very near by this: he was not three leagues off when I left him.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: How many gentlemen have you lost in this action?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: But few of any sort, and none of name.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: A victory is twice itself when the achiever brings home full

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: numbers. I find here that Don Pedro hath bestowed much honour on a

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: young Florentine called Claudio.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Much deserved on his part, and equally remembered by Don Pedro.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He hath borne himself beyond the promise of his age, doing in the figure

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: of a lamb the feats of a lion: he hath indeed better bettered expectation

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: than you must expect of me to tell you how.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: He hath an uncle here in Messina will be very much glad of it.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I have already delivered him letters, and there appears much

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: joy in him; even so much that joy could not show itself modest enough

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: without a badge of bitterness.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Did he break out into tears?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: In great measure.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: A kind overflow of kindness. There are no faces truer than those

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: that are so washed; how much better is it to weep at joy than to joy at

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: weeping!

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I pray you, is Signior Mountanto returned from the wars or no?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I know none of that name, lady: there was none such in the army

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: of any sort.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What is he that you ask for, niece?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: My cousin means Signior Benedick of Padua.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: O! he is returned, and as pleasant as ever he was.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: He set up his bills here in Messina and challenged Cupid at the

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: flight; and my uncle’s fool, reading the challenge, subscribed for

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Cupid, and challenged him at the bird-bolt. I pray you, how many hath he

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: killed and eaten in these wars? But how many hath he killed? for, indeed,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I promised to eat all of his killing.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Faith, niece, you tax Signior Benedick too much; but he’ll

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: be meet with you, I doubt it not.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He hath done good service, lady, in these wars.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: You had musty victual, and he hath holp to eat it; he is a very

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: valiant trencher-man; he hath an excellent stomach.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And a good soldier too, lady.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: And a good soldier to a lady; but what is he to a lord?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A lord to a lord, a man to a man; stuffed with all honourable

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: virtues.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: It is so indeed; he is no less than a stuffed man; but for the

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: stuffing,—well, we are all mortal.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: You must not, sir, mistake my niece. There is a kind of merry war

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: betwixt Signior Benedick and her; they never meet but there’s a

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: skirmish of wit between them.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Alas! he gets nothing by that. In our last conflict four of his

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: five wits went halting off, and now is the whole man governed with one! so

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: that if he have wit enough to keep himself warm, let him bear it for a

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: difference between himself and his horse; for it is all the wealth that he

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: hath left to be known a reasonable creature. Who is his companion now? He

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: hath every month a new sworn brother.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Is’t possible?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Very easily possible: he wears his faith but as the fashion of

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: his hat; it ever changes with the next block.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I see, lady, the gentleman is not in your books.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No; and he were, I would burn my study. But I pray you, who is

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: his companion? Is there no young squarer now that will make a voyage with

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: him to the devil?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He is most in the company of the right noble Claudio.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: O Lord, he will hang upon him like a disease: he is sooner

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: caught than the pestilence, and the taker runs presently mad. God help the

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: noble Claudio! If he have caught the Benedick, it will cost him a thousand

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: pound ere he be cured.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I will hold friends with you, lady.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Do, good friend.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: You will never run mad, niece.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No, not till a hot January.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Don Pedro is approached.
Enter Don Pedro, Don John, Claudio, Benedick, Balthasar and Others.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Good Signior Leonato, you are come to meet your trouble: the

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: fashion of the world is to avoid cost, and you encounter it.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Never came trouble to my house in the likeness of your Grace, for

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: trouble being gone, comfort should remain; but when you depart from me,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: sorrow abides and happiness takes his leave.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: You embrace your charge too willingly. I think this is

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: your daughter.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Her mother hath many times told me so.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Were you in doubt, sir, that you asked her?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Signior Benedick, no; for then were you a child.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: You have it full, Benedick: we may guess by this what you are,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: being a man. Truly the lady fathers herself. Be happy, lady, for you are

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: like an honourable father.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: If Signior Leonato be her father, she would not have his head on

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: her shoulders for all Messina, as like him as she is.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I wonder that you will still be talking, Signior Benedick:

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: nobody marks you.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: What! my dear Lady Disdain, are you yet living?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Is it possible Disdain should die while she hath such meet food

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: to feed it as Signior Benedick? Courtesy itself must convert to disdain if

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: you come in her presence.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Then is courtesy a turncoat. But it is certain I am loved of all

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ladies, only you excepted; and I would I could find in my heart that I had

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: not a hard heart; for, truly, I love none.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: A dear happiness to women: they would else have been troubled

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: with a pernicious suitor. I thank God and my cold blood, I am of your

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: humour for that. I had rather hear my dog bark at a crow than a man swear

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: he loves me.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: God keep your Ladyship still in that mind; so some gentleman or

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: other shall scape a predestinate scratched face.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Scratching could not make it worse, and ’twere such a face

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: as yours were.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Well, you are a rare parrot-teacher.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: A bird of my tongue is better than a beast of yours.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I would my horse had the speed of your tongue, and so good a

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: continuer. But keep your way, i’ God’s name; I have done.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: You always end with a jade’s trick: I know you of old.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: That is the sum of all, Leonato: Signior Claudio, and Signior

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Benedick, my dear friend Leonato hath invited you all. I tell him we shall

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: stay here at the least a month, and he heartly prays some occasion may

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: detain us longer: I dare swear he is no hypocrite, but prays from his

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: heart.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: If you swear, my lord, you shall not be forsworn. [To

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Don John] Let me bid you welcome, my lord: being reconciled to

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: the Prince your brother, I owe you all duty.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I thank you: I am not of many words, but I thank you.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Please it your Grace lead on?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Your hand, Leonato; we will go together.
[Exeunt all but Benedick and Claudio.]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Benedick, didst thou note the daughter of Signior Leonato?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I noted her not; but I looked on her.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Is she not a modest young lady?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Do you question me, as an honest man should do, for my simple

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: true judgment; or would you have me speak after my custom, as being a

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: professed tyrant to their sex?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: No; I pray thee speak in sober judgment.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Why, i’ faith, methinks she’s too low for a high

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: praise, too brown for a fair praise, and too little for a great praise;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: only this commendation I can afford her, that were she other than she is,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: she were unhandsome, and being no other but as she is, I do not like her.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Thou thinkest I am in sport: I pray thee tell me truly how thou

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: likest her.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Would you buy her, that you enquire after her?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Can the world buy such a jewel?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Yea, and a case to put it into. But speak you this with a sad

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: brow, or do you play the flouting Jack, to tell us Cupid is a good

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: hare-finder, and Vulcan a rare carpenter? Come, in what key shall a man

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: take you, to go in the song?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: In mine eye she is the sweetest lady that ever I looked on.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I can see yet without spectacles and I see no such matter: there’s

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: her cousin and she were not possessed with a fury, exceeds her as much in

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: beauty as the first of May doth the last of December. But I hope you have

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: no intent to turn husband, have you?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I would scarce trust myself, though I had sworn to the contrary,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: if Hero would be my wife.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Is’t come to this, in faith? Hath not the world one

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: man but he will wear his cap with suspicion? Shall I never see a bachelor

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: of threescore again? Go to, i’ faith; and thou wilt needs thrust thy

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: neck into a yoke, wear the print of it and sigh away Sundays.
Re-enter Don Pedro.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Look! Don Pedro is returned to seek you.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What secret hath held you here, that you followed not to

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Leonato’s?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I would your Grace would constrain me to tell.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I charge thee on thy allegiance.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: You hear, Count Claudio: I can be secret as a dumb man; I would

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: have you think so; but on my allegiance mark you this, on my allegiance:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: he is in love. With who? now that is your Grace’s part. Mark how

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: short his answer is: with Hero, Leonato’s short daughter.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If this were so, so were it uttered.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Like the old tale, my lord: ‘it is not so, nor

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ’twas not so; but indeed, God forbid it should be so.’

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If my passion change not shortly, God forbid it should be otherwise.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Amen, if you love her; for the lady is very well worthy.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: You speak this to fetch me in, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: By my troth, I speak my thought.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And in faith, my lord, I spoke mine.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And by my two faiths and troths, my lord, I spoke mine.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That I love her, I feel.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: That she is worthy, I know.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: That I neither feel how she should be loved, nor know how she

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: should be worthy, is the opinion that fire cannot melt out of me: I will

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: die in it at the stake.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Thou wast ever an obstinate heretic in the despite of beauty.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And never could maintain his part but in the force of his will.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: That a woman conceived me, I thank her; that she brought me up,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I likewise give her most humble thanks; but that I will have a recheat

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: winded in my forehead, or hang my bugle in an invisible baldrick, all

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: women shall pardon me. Because I will not do them the wrong to mistrust

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: any, I will do myself the right to trust none; and the fine is,—for the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: which I may go the finer,—I will live a bachelor.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I shall see thee, ere I die, look pale with love.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: With anger, with sickness, or with hunger, my lord; not with

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: love: prove that ever I lose more blood with love than I will get again

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: with drinking, pick out mine eyes with a ballad-maker’s pen and hang

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: me up at the door of a brothel-house for the sign of blind Cupid.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Well, if ever thou dost fall from this faith, thou wilt prove a

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: notable argument.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: If I do, hang me in a bottle like a cat and shoot at me; and he

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: that hits me, let him be clapped on the shoulder and called Adam.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Well, as time shall try: ‘In time the savage bull

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: doth bear the yoke.’

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: The savage bull may; but if ever the sensible Benedick bear it,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: pluck off the bull’s horns and set them in my forehead; and let me

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: be vilely painted, and in such great letters as they write, ‘Here is

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: good horse to hire,’ let them signify under my sign ‘Here you

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: may see Benedick the married man.’

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If this should ever happen, thou wouldst be horn-mad.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Nay, if Cupid have not spent all his quiver in Venice, thou

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: wilt quake for this shortly.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I look for an earthquake too then.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Well, you will temporize with the hours. In the meantime,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: good Signior Benedick, repair to Leonato’s: commend me to him

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: and tell him I will not fail him at supper; for indeed he hath made

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: great preparation.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I have almost matter enough in me for such an embassage; and so

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I commit you—

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: To the tuition of God: from my house, if I had it,—

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: The sixth of July: your loving friend, Benedick.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Nay, mock not, mock not. The body of your discourse is sometime

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: guarded with fragments, and the guards are but slightly basted on neither:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ere you flout old ends any further, examine your conscience: and so I

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: leave you.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: My liege, your Highness now may do me good.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: My love is thine to teach: teach it but how,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And thou shalt see how apt it is to learn

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Any hard lesson that may do thee good.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Hath Leonato any son, my lord?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: No child but Hero; she’s his only heir.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Dost thou affect her, Claudio?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O! my lord,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: When you went onward on this ended action,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I looked upon her with a soldier’s eye,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That lik’d, but had a rougher task in hand

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Than to drive liking to the name of love;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But now I am return’d, and that war-thoughts

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Have left their places vacant, in their rooms

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Come thronging soft and delicate desires,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: All prompting me how fair young Hero is,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Saying, I lik’d her ere I went to wars.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Thou wilt be like a lover presently,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And tire the hearer with a book of words.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: If thou dost love fair Hero, cherish it,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And I will break with her, and with her father,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And thou shalt have her. Was’t not to this end

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: That thou began’st to twist so fine a story?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: How sweetly you do minister to love,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That know love’s grief by his complexion!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But lest my liking might too sudden seem,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I would have salv’d it with a longer treatise.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What need the bridge much broader than the flood?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: The fairest grant is the necessity.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Look, what will serve is fit: ’tis once, thou lov’st,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And I will fit thee with the remedy.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I know we shall have revelling tonight:

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I will assume thy part in some disguise,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And tell fair Hero I am Claudio;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And in her bosom I’ll unclasp my heart,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And take her hearing prisoner with the force

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And strong encounter of my amorous tale:

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Then after to her father will I break;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And the conclusion is, she shall be thine.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: In practice let us put it presently.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Leonato and Antonio, meeting.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: How now, brother? Where is my cousin your son? Hath he provided

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: this music?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: He is very busy about it. But, brother, I can tell you strange

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: news that you yet dreamt not of.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Are they good?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: As the event stamps them: but they have a good cover; they show

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: well outward. The Prince and Count Claudio, walking in a thick-pleached

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: alley in my orchard, were thus much overheard by a man of mine: the Prince

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: discovered to Claudio that he loved my niece your daughter and meant to

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: acknowledge it this night in a dance; and if he found her accordant, he

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: meant to take the present time by the top and instantly break with you of

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: it.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Hath the fellow any wit that told you this?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: A good sharp fellow: I will send for him; and question him yourself.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No, no; we will hold it as a dream till it appear itself: but I

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: will acquaint my daughter withal, that she may be the better prepared for

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: an answer, if peradventure this be true. Go you and tell her of it.
[Several persons cross the stage.]

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Cousins, you know what you have to do. O! I cry you mercy, friend; go you

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: with me, and I will use your skill. Good cousin, have a care this busy

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: time.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Don John and Conrade.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: What the good-year, my lord! why are you thus out of measure sad?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: There is no measure in the occasion that breeds; therefore the

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: sadness is without limit.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: You should hear reason.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: And when I have heard it, what blessings brings it?

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: If not a present remedy, at least a patient sufferance.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I wonder that thou (being as thou say’st thou art, born

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: under Saturn) goest about to apply a moral medicine to a mortifying

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: mischief. I cannot hide what I am: I must be sad when I have cause, and

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: smile at no man’s jests; eat when I have stomach, and wait for no

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: man’s leisure; sleep when I am drowsy, and tend on no man’s

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: business; laugh when I am merry, and claw no man in his humour.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Yea; but you must not make the full show of this till you may do

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: it without controlment. You have of late stood out against your brother,

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: and he hath ta’en you newly into his grace; where it is impossible

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: you should take true root but by the fair weather that you make yourself:

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: it is needful that you frame the season for your own harvest.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I had rather be a canker in a hedge than a rose in his grace;

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: and it better fits my blood to be disdained of all than to fashion a

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: carriage to rob love from any: in this, though I cannot be said to be a

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: flattering honest man, it must not be denied but I am a plain-dealing

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: villain. I am trusted with a muzzle and enfranchised with a clog;

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: therefore I have decreed not to sing in my cage. If I had my mouth, I

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: would bite; if I had my liberty, I would do my liking: in the meantime,

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: let me be that I am, and seek not to alter me.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Can you make no use of your discontent?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I make all use of it, for I use it only. Who comes here?
Enter Borachio.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: What news, Borachio?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: I came yonder from a great supper: the Prince your brother is

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: royally entertained by Leonato; and I can give you intelligence of an

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: intended marriage.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Will it serve for any model to build mischief on? What is he for

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: a fool that betroths himself to unquietness?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Marry, it is your brother’s right hand.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Who? the most exquisite Claudio?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Even he.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: A proper squire! And who, and who? which way looks he?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Marry, on Hero, the daughter and heir of Leonato.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: A very forward March-chick! How came you to this?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Being entertained for a perfumer, as I was smoking a musty room,

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: comes me the Prince and Claudio, hand in hand, in sad conference: I whipt

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: me behind the arras, and there heard it agreed upon that the Prince should

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: woo Hero for himself, and having obtained her, give her to Count Claudio.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Come, come; let us thither: this may prove food to my

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: displeasure. That young start-up hath all the glory of my overthrow: if I

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: can cross him any way, I bless myself every way. You are both sure, and

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: will assist me?

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: To the death, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Let us to the great supper: their cheer is the greater that I am

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: subdued. Would the cook were of my mind! Shall we go to prove what’s

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: to be done?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: We’ll wait upon your Lordship.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Leonato, Antonio, Hero, Beatrice and others.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Was not Count John here at supper?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: I saw him not.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: How tartly that gentleman looks! I never can see him but I am

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: heart-burned an hour after.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: He is of a very melancholy disposition.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: He were an excellent man that were made just in the mid-way

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: between him and Benedick: the one is too like an image, and says nothing;

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and the other too like my lady’s eldest son, evermore tattling.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Then half Signior Benedick’s tongue in Count John’s

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: mouth, and half Count John’s melancholy in Signior Benedick’s

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: face—

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: With a good leg and a good foot, uncle, and money enough in his

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: purse, such a man would win any woman in the world if a’ could get

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: her good will.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: By my troth, niece, thou wilt never get thee a husband, if thou

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: be so shrewd of thy tongue.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: In faith, she’s too curst.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Too curst is more than curst: I shall lessen God’s sending

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: that way; for it is said, ‘God sends a curst cow short horns;’

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: but to a cow too curst he sends none.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: So, by being too curst, God will send you no horns?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Just, if he send me no husband; for the which blessing I am at

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: him upon my knees every morning and evening. Lord! I could not endure a

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: husband with a beard on his face: I had rather lie in the woollen.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: You may light on a husband that hath no beard.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: What should I do with him? dress him in my apparel and make him

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: my waiting gentlewoman? He that hath a beard is more than a youth, and he

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: that hath no beard is less than a man; and he that is more than a youth is

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: not for me; and he that is less than a man, I am not for him: therefore I

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: will even take sixpence in earnest of the bear-ward, and lead his apes

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: into hell.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Well then, go you into hell?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No; but to the gate; and there will the Devil meet me, like an

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: old cuckold, with horns on his head, and say, ‘Get you to heaven,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Beatrice, get you to heaven; here’s no place for you maids.’ So

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: deliver I up my apes, and away to Saint Peter for the heavens: he shows me

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: where the bachelors sit, and there live we as merry as the day is long.
[To Hero.]

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Well, niece, I trust you will be ruled by your father.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Yes, faith; it is my cousin’s duty to make curtsy,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and say, ‘Father, as it please you:’— but yet for all

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: that, cousin, let him be a handsome fellow, or else make another

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: curtsy, and say, ‘Father, as it please me.’

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Well, niece, I hope to see you one day fitted with a husband.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Not till God make men of some other metal than earth. Would it

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: not grieve a woman to be over-mastered with a piece of valiant dust? to

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: make an account of her life to a clod of wayward marl? No, uncle, I’ll

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: none: Adam’s sons are my brethren; and truly, I hold it a sin to

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: match in my kindred.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Daughter, remember what I told you: if the Prince do solicit you

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: in that kind, you know your answer.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: The fault will be in the music, cousin, if you be not wooed in

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: good time: if the Prince be too important, tell him there is measure in

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: everything, and so dance out the answer. For, hear me, Hero: wooing,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: wedding, and repenting is as a Scotch jig, a measure, and a cinquepace:

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: the first suit is hot and hasty, like a Scotch jig, and full as

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: fantastical; the wedding, mannerly modest, as a measure, full of state and

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: ancientry; and then comes Repentance, and with his bad legs, falls into

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: the cinquepace faster and faster, till he sink into his grave.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Cousin, you apprehend passing shrewdly.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I have a good eye, uncle: I can see a church by daylight.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The revellers are entering, brother: make good room.
Enter Don Pedro, Claudio, Benedick, Balthasar, Don John, Borachio, Margaret, Ursula and Others, masked.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Lady, will you walk about with your friend?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: So you walk softly and look sweetly and say nothing, I am yours for

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: the walk; and especially when I walk away.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: With me in your company?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: I may say so, when I please.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And when please you to say so?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: When I like your favour; for God defend the lute should be like the case!

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: My visor is Philemon’s roof; within the house is Jove.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Why, then, your visor should be thatch’d.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Speak low, if you speak love.
[Takes her aside.]

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Well, I would you did like me.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: So would not I, for your own sake; for I have many ill qualities.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Which is one?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: I say my prayers aloud.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: I love you the better; the hearers may cry Amen.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: God match me with a good dancer!

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Amen.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: And God keep him out of my sight when the dance is done! Answer, clerk.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: No more words: the clerk is answered.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: I know you well enough: you are Signior Antonio.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: At a word, I am not.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: I know you by the waggling of your head.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: To tell you true, I counterfeit him.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: You could never do him so ill-well, unless you were the very

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: man. Here’s his dry hand up and down: you are he, you are he.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: At a word, I am not.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Come, come; do you think I do not know you by your excellent

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: wit? Can virtue hide itself? Go to, mum, you are he: graces will

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: appear, and there’s an end.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Will you not tell me who told you so?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: No, you shall pardon me.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Nor will you not tell me who you are?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Not now.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: That I was disdainful, and that I had my good wit out of

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: the ‘Hundred Merry Tales.’ Well, this was Signior

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Benedick that said so.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: What’s he?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I am sure you know him well enough.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Not I, believe me.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Did he never make you laugh?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I pray you, what is he?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Why, he is the Prince’s jester: a very dull fool; only his

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: gift is in devising impossible slanders: none but libertines delight in

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: him; and the commendation is not in his wit, but in his villainy; for he

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: both pleases men and angers them, and then they laugh at him and beat him.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I am sure he is in the fleet: I would he had boarded me!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: When I know the gentleman, I’ll tell him what you say.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Do, do: he’ll but break a comparison or two on me; which,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: peradventure not marked or not laughed at, strikes him into melancholy;

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and then there’s a partridge wing saved, for the fool will eat no

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: supper that night. [Music within.] We must follow the leaders.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: In every good thing.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Nay, if they lead to any ill, I will leave them at the next turning.
[Dance. Then exeunt all but Don John, Borachio and Claudio.]

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Sure my brother is amorous on Hero, and hath withdrawn her

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: father to break with him about it. The ladies follow her and but one visor

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: remains.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: And that is Claudio: I know him by his bearing.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Are you not Signior Benedick?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: You know me well; I am he.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Signior, you are very near my brother in his love: he is

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: enamoured on Hero; I pray you, dissuade him from her; she is no equal for

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: his birth: you may do the part of an honest man in it.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: How know you he loves her?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I heard him swear his affection.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: So did I too; and he swore he would marry her tonight.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Come, let us to the banquet.
[Exeunt Don John and Borachio.]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Thus answer I in name of Benedick,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But hear these ill news with the ears of Claudio.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: ’Tis certain so; the Prince wooss for himself.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Friendship is constant in all other things

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Save in the office and affairs of love:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Therefore all hearts in love use their own tongues;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Let every eye negotiate for itself

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And trust no agent; for beauty is a witch

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Against whose charms faith melteth into blood.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: This is an accident of hourly proof,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Which I mistrusted not. Farewell, therefore, Hero!
Re-enter Benedick.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Count Claudio?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yea, the same.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Come, will you go with me?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Whither?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Even to the next willow, about your own business, Count. What

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: fashion will you wear the garland of? About your neck, like a usurer’s

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: chain? or under your arm, like a lieutenant’s scarf? You must wear

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: it one way, for the Prince hath got your Hero.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I wish him joy of her.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Why, that’s spoken like an honest drovier: so they sell bullocks.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: But did you think the Prince would have served you thus?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I pray you, leave me.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Ho! now you strike like the blind man: ’twas the boy that

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: stole your meat, and you’ll beat the post.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If it will not be, I’ll leave you.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Alas! poor hurt fowl. Now will he creep into sedges. But, that

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: my Lady Beatrice should know me, and not know me! The Prince’s fool!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Ha! it may be I go under that title because I am merry. Yea, but so I am

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: apt to do myself wrong; I am not so reputed: it is the base though bitter

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: disposition of Beatrice that puts the world into her person, and so gives

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: me out. Well, I’ll be revenged as I may.
Re-enter Don Pedro.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Now, signior, where’s the Count? Did you see him?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Troth, my lord, I have played the part of Lady Fame. I found him

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: here as melancholy as a lodge in a warren. I told him, and I think I told

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: him true, that your Grace had got the good will of this young lady; and I

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: offered him my company to a willow tree, either to make him a garland, as

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: being forsaken, or to bind him up a rod, as being worthy to be whipped.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: To be whipped! What’s his fault?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: The flat transgression of a school-boy, who, being overjoy’d

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: with finding a bird’s nest, shows it his companion, and he steals

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: it.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Wilt thou make a trust a transgression? The transgression is in the stealer.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Yet it had not been amiss the rod had been made, and the garland

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: too; for the garland he might have worn himself, and the rod he might have

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: bestowed on you, who, as I take it, have stolen his bird’s nest.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I will but teach them to sing, and restore them to the owner.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: If their singing answer your saying, by my faith, you say honestly.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: The Lady Beatrice hath a quarrel to you: the gentleman that

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: danced with her told her she is much wronged by you.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: O! she misused me past the endurance of a block: an oak but with

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: one green leaf on it would have answered her: my very visor began to

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: assume life and scold with her. She told me, not thinking I had been

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: myself, that I was the Prince’s jester, that I was duller than a

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: great thaw; huddling jest upon jest with such impossible conveyance upon

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: me, that I stood like a man at a mark, with a whole army shooting at me.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: She speaks poniards, and every word stabs: if her breath were as terrible

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: as her terminations, there were no living near her; she would infect to

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: the north star. I would not marry her, though she were endowed with all

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: that Adam had left him before he transgressed: she would have made

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Hercules have turned spit, yea, and have cleft his club to make the fire

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: too. Come, talk not of her; you shall find her the infernal Ate in good

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: apparel. I would to God some scholar would conjure her, for certainly,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: while she is here, a man may live as quiet in hell as in a sanctuary; and

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: people sin upon purpose because they would go thither; so indeed, all

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: disquiet, horror and perturbation follow her.
Re-enter Claudio, Beatrice, Hero and Leonato.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Look! here she comes.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Will your Grace command me any service to the world’s end?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I will go on the slightest errand now to the Antipodes that you can devise

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: to send me on; I will fetch you a toothpicker now from the furthest inch

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: of Asia; bring you the length of Prester John’s foot; fetch you a

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: hair off the Great Cham’s beard; do you any embassage to the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Pygmies, rather than hold three words’ conference with this harpy.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: You have no employment for me?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: None, but to desire your good company.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: O God, sir, here’s a dish I love not: I cannot endure my Lady Tongue.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Come, lady, come; you have lost the heart of Signior Benedick.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Indeed, my lord, he lent it me awhile; and I gave him use for

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: it, a double heart for a single one: marry, once before he won it of me

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: with false dice, therefore your Grace may well say I have lost it.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: You have put him down, lady, you have put him down.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: So I would not he should do me, my lord, lest I should prove the

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: mother of fools. I have brought Count Claudio, whom you sent me to seek.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Why, how now, Count! wherefore are you sad?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Not sad, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: How then? Sick?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Neither, my lord.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: The Count is neither sad, nor sick, nor merry, nor well; but

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: civil Count, civil as an orange, and something of that jealous complexion.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I’ faith, lady, I think your blazon to be true; though, I’ll

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: be sworn, if he be so, his conceit is false. Here, Claudio, I have wooed

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: in thy name, and fair Hero is won; I have broke with her father, and, his

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: good will obtained; name the day of marriage, and God give thee joy!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Count, take of me my daughter, and with her my fortunes: his

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Grace hath made the match, and all grace say Amen to it!

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Speak, Count, ’tis your cue.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Silence is the perfectest herald of joy: I were but little happy,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: if I could say how much. Lady, as you are mine, I am yours: I give away

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: myself for you and dote upon the exchange.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Speak, cousin; or, if you cannot, stop his mouth with a kiss,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and let not him speak neither.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: In faith, lady, you have a merry heart.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Yea, my lord; I thank it, poor fool, it keeps on the windy

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: side of care. My cousin tells him in his ear that he is in her heart.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And so she doth, cousin.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Good Lord, for alliance! Thus goes everyone to the world but I,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and I am sunburnt. I may sit in a corner and cry heigh-ho for a husband!

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Lady Beatrice, I will get you one.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I would rather have one of your father’s getting. Hath

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: your Grace ne’er a brother like you? Your father got excellent

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: husbands, if a maid could come by them.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Will you have me, lady?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No, my lord, unless I might have another for working days:

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: your Grace is too costly to wear every day. But, I beseech your

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Grace, pardon me; I was born to speak all mirth and no matter.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Your silence most offends me, and to be merry best becomes you;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: for out of question, you were born in a merry hour.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No, sure, my lord, my mother cried; but then there was a star

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: danced, and under that was I born. Cousins, God give you joy!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Niece, will you look to those things I told you of?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I cry you mercy, uncle. By your Grace’s pardon.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: By my troth, a pleasant spirited lady.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: There’s little of the melancholy element in her, my lord:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: she is never sad but when she sleeps; and not ever sad then, for I have

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: heard my daughter say, she hath often dreamed of unhappiness and waked

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: herself with laughing.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: She cannot endure to hear tell of a husband.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O! by no means: she mocks all her wooers out of suit.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: She were an excellent wife for Benedick.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O Lord! my lord, if they were but a week married, they would talk

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: themselves mad.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Count Claudio, when mean you to go to church?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Tomorrow, my lord. Time goes on crutches till love have all his rites.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Not till Monday, my dear son, which is hence a just seven-night;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: and a time too brief too, to have all things answer my mind.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Come, you shake the head at so long a breathing; but, I warrant

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: thee, Claudio, the time shall not go dully by us. I will in the interim

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: undertake one of Hercules’ labours, which is, to bring Signior

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Benedick and the Lady Beatrice into a mountain of affection the one with

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: the other. I would fain have it a match; and I doubt not but to fashion

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: it, if you three will but minister such assistance as I shall give you

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: direction.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My lord, I am for you, though it cost me ten nights’

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: watchings.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And I, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And you too, gentle Hero?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: I will do any modest office, my lord, to help my cousin to a good

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: husband.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And Benedick is not the unhopefullest husband that I know. Thus

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: far can I praise him; he is of a noble strain, of approved valour, and

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: confirmed honesty. I will teach you how to humour your cousin, that she

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: shall fall in love with Benedick; and I, with your two helps, will so

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: practise on Benedick that, in despite of his quick wit and his queasy

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: stomach, he shall fall in love with Beatrice. If we can do this, Cupid is

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: no longer an archer: his glory shall be ours, for we are the only

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: love-gods. Go in with me, and I will tell you my drift.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Don John and Borachio.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: It is so; the Count Claudio shall marry the daughter of Leonato.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Yea, my lord; but I can cross it.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Any bar, any cross, any impediment will be medicinable to me: I

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: am sick in displeasure to him, and whatsoever comes athwart his affection

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: ranges evenly with mine. How canst thou cross this marriage?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Not honestly, my lord; but so covertly that no dishonesty shall

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: appear in me.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Show me briefly how.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: I think I told your lordship, a year since, how much I am in the

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: favour of Margaret, the waiting gentlewoman to Hero.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I remember.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: I can, at any unseasonable instant of the night, appoint her to

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: look out at her lady’s chamber window.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: What life is in that, to be the death of this marriage?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: The poison of that lies in you to temper. Go you to the Prince

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: your brother; spare not to tell him, that he hath wronged his honour in

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: marrying the renowned Claudio,—whose estimation do you mightily hold

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: up,—to a contaminated stale, such a one as Hero.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: What proof shall I make of that?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Proof enough to misuse the Prince, to vex Claudio, to undo Hero,

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: and kill Leonato. Look you for any other issue?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Only to despite them, I will endeavour anything.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Go then; find me a meet hour to draw Don Pedro and the Count

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Claudio alone: tell them that you know that Hero loves me; intend a kind

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: of zeal both to the Prince and Claudio, as—in love of your brother’s

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: honour, who hath made this match, and his friend’s reputation, who

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: is thus like to be cozened with the semblance of a maid,—that you have

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: discovered thus. They will scarcely believe this without trial: offer them

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: instances, which shall bear no less likelihood than to see me at her

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: chamber window, hear me call Margaret Hero, hear Margaret term me Claudio;

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: and bring them to see this the very night before the intended wedding: for

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: in the meantime I will so fashion the matter that Hero shall be absent;

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: and there shall appear such seeming truth of Hero’s disloyalty, that

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: jealousy shall be called assurance, and all the preparation overthrown.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Grow this to what adverse issue it can, I will put it in practice. Be

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: cunning in the working this, and thy fee is a thousand ducats.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Be you constant in the accusation, and my cunning shall not shame me.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I will presently go learn their day of marriage.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Benedick.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Boy!
Enter a Boy.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Signior?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: In my chamber window lies a book; bring it hither to me in the orchard.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: I am here already, sir.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I know that; but I would have thee hence, and here again.
[Exit Boy.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I do much wonder that one man, seeing how much another man is a fool when

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: he dedicates his behaviours to love, will, after he hath laughed at such

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: shallow follies in others, become the argument of his own scorn by falling

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: in love: and such a man is Claudio. I have known, when there was no music

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: with him but the drum and the fife; and now had he rather hear the tabor

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: and the pipe: I have known when he would have walked ten mile afoot to see

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: a good armour; and now will he lie ten nights awake, carving the fashion

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: of a new doublet. He was wont to speak plain and to the purpose, like an

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: honest man and a soldier; and now is he turned orthography; his words are

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: a very fantastical banquet, just so many strange dishes. May I be so

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: converted, and see with these eyes? I cannot tell; I think not: I will not

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: be sworn but love may transform me to an oyster; but I’ll take my

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: oath on it, till he have made an oyster of me, he shall never make me such

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: a fool. One woman is fair, yet I am well; another is wise, yet I am well;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: another virtuous, yet I am well; but till all graces be in one woman, one

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: woman shall not come in my grace. Rich she shall be, that’s certain;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: wise, or I’ll none; virtuous, or I’ll never cheapen her; fair,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: or I’ll never look on her; mild, or come not near me; noble, or not

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I for an angel; of good discourse, an excellent musician, and her hair

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: shall be of what colour it please God. Ha! the Prince and Monsieur Love! I

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: will hide me in the arbour.
[Withdraws.]
Enter Don Pedro, Leonato and Claudio, followed by Balthasar and Musicians.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Come, shall we hear this music?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yea, my good lord. How still the evening is,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: As hush’d on purpose to grace harmony!

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: See you where Benedick hath hid himself?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O! very well, my lord: the music ended,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: We’ll fit the kid-fox with a penny-worth.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Come, Balthasar, we’ll hear that song again.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: O! good my lord, tax not so bad a voice

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: To slander music any more than once.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: It is the witness still of excellency,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: To put a strange face on his own perfection.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I pray thee, sing, and let me woo no more.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Because you talk of wooing, I will sing;

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Since many a wooer doth commence his suit

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: To her he thinks not worthy; yet he wooes;

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Yet will he swear he loves.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Nay, pray thee come;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Or if thou wilt hold longer argument,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Do it in notes.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Note this before my notes;

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: There’s not a note of mine that’s worth the noting.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Why these are very crotchets that he speaks;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Notes, notes, forsooth, and nothing!
[Music.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Now, divine air! now is his soul ravished! Is it not strange

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: that sheep’s guts should hale souls out of men’s bodies? Well,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: a horn for my money, when all’s done.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: BALTHASAR
[sings.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Sigh no more, ladies, sigh no more,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Men were deceivers ever;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: One foot in sea, and one on shore,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: To one thing constant never.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Then sigh not so, but let them go,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And be you blithe and bonny,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Converting all your sounds of woe

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Into Hey nonny, nonny.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Sing no more ditties, sing no mo

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Of dumps so dull and heavy;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: The fraud of men was ever so,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Since summer first was leavy.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Then sigh not so, but let them go,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And be you blithe and bonny,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Converting all your sounds of woe

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Into Hey nonny, nonny.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: By my troth, a good song.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And an ill singer, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Ha, no, no, faith; thou singest well enough for a shift.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And he had been a dog that should have howled

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: thus, they would have hanged him; and I pray God his bad voice bode no

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: mischief. I had as lief have heard the night-raven, come what plague could

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: have come after it.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Yea, marry; dost thou hear, Balthasar? I pray thee, get us

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: some excellent music, for tomorrow night we would have it at the

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Lady Hero’s chamber window.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: The best I can, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Do so: farewell.
[Exeunt Balthasar and Musicians.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Come hither, Leonato: what was it you told me of today, that your niece

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Beatrice was in love with Signior Benedick?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O! ay:—[Aside to Don Pedro] Stalk on, stalk on;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: the fowl sits. I did never think that lady would have loved any man.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No, nor I neither; but most wonderful that she should so

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: dote on Signior Benedick, whom she hath in all outward behaviours

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: seemed ever to abhor.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Is’t possible? Sits the wind in that corner?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: By my troth, my lord, I cannot tell what to think of it but that

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: she loves him with an enraged affection: it is past the infinite of

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: thought.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Maybe she doth but counterfeit.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Faith, like enough.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O God! counterfeit! There was never counterfeit of passion came

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: so near the life of passion as she discovers it.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Why, what effects of passion shows she?
[Aside]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Bait the hook well: this fish will bite.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What effects, my lord? She will sit you; [To Claudio] You

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: heard my daughter tell you how.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: She did, indeed.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: How, how, I pray you? You amaze me: I would have thought her

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: spirit had been invincible against all assaults of affection.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I would have sworn it had, my lord; especially against Benedick.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I should think this a gull, but that the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: white-bearded fellow speaks it: knavery cannot, sure, hide itself in such

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: reverence.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: He hath ta’en the infection: hold it

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: up.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Hath she made her affection known to Benedick?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No; and swears she never will: that’s her torment.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: ’Tis true, indeed; so your daughter says: ‘Shall I,’

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: says she, ‘that have so oft encountered him with scorn, write to him

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: that I love him?’

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: This says she now when she is beginning to write to him; for she’ll

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: be up twenty times a night, and there will she sit in her smock till she

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: have writ a sheet of paper: my daughter tells us all.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Now you talk of a sheet of paper, I remember a pretty jest your

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: daughter told us of.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O! when she had writ it, and was reading it over, she found

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Benedick and Beatrice between the sheet?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O! she tore the letter into a thousand halfpence; railed at

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: herself, that she should be so immodest to write to one that she knew

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: would flout her: ‘I measure him,’ says she, ‘by my own

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: spirit; for I should flout him, if he writ to me; yea, though I love him,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I should.’

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Then down upon her knees she falls, weeps, sobs, beats her heart,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: tears her hair, prays, curses; ‘O sweet Benedick! God give me

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: patience!’

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: She doth indeed; my daughter says so; and the ecstasy hath so

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: much overborne her, that my daughter is sometimes afeard she will do a

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: desperate outrage to herself. It is very true.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: It were good that Benedick knew of it by some other, if she

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: will not discover it.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: To what end? he would make but a sport of it and torment the poor

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: lady worse.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And he should, it were an alms to hang him. She’s an

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: excellent sweet lady, and, out of all suspicion, she is virtuous.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And she is exceeding wise.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: In everything but in loving Benedick.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O! my lord, wisdom and blood combating in so tender a body,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: we have ten proofs to one that blood hath the victory. I am sorry for

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: her, as I have just cause, being her uncle and her guardian.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I would she had bestowed this dotage on me; I would have daffed

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: all other respects and made her half myself. I pray you, tell Benedick of

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: it, and hear what he will say.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Were it good, think you?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Hero thinks surely she will die; for she says she will die if he

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: love her not, and she will die ere she make her love known, and she will

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: die if he woo her, rather than she will bate one breath of her accustomed

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: crossness.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: She doth well: if she should make tender of her love, ’tis

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: very possible he’ll scorn it; for the man,—as you know all,—hath a

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: contemptible spirit.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: He is a very proper man.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: He hath indeed a good outward happiness.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: ’Fore God, and in my mind, very wise.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: He doth indeed show some sparks that are like wit.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And I take him to be valiant.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: As Hector, I assure you: and in the managing of quarrels you

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: may say he is wise; for either he avoids them with great discretion, or

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: undertakes them with a most Christian-like fear.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: If he do fear God, a’ must necessarily keep peace: if he

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: break the peace, he ought to enter into a quarrel with fear and trembling.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And so will he do; for the man doth fear God, howsoever it

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: seems not in him by some large jests he will make. Well, I am sorry for

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: your niece. Shall we go seek Benedick and tell him of her love?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Never tell him, my lord: let her wear it out with good counsel.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Nay, that’s impossible: she may wear her heart out first.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Well, we will hear further of it by your daughter: let it cool

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: the while. I love Benedick well, and I could wish he would modestly

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: examine himself, to see how much he is unworthy so good a lady.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My lord, will you walk? dinner is ready.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If he do not dote on her upon this, I will never

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: trust my expectation.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Let there be the same net spread for her; and

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: that must your daughter and her gentlewoman carry. The sport will be,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: when they hold one an opinion of another’s dotage, and no such

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: matter: that’s the scene that I would see, which will be merely a

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: dumb show. Let us send her to call him in to dinner.
[Exeunt Don Pedro, Claudio and Leonato.]
[Advancing from the arbour.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: This can be no trick: the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: conference was sadly borne. They have the truth of this from Hero. They

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: seem to pity the lady: it seems her affections have their full bent. Love

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: me? why, it must be requited. I hear how I am censured: they say I will

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: bear myself proudly, if I perceive the love come from her; they say too

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: that she will rather die than give any sign of affection. I did never

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: think to marry: I must not seem proud: happy are they that hear their

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: detractions, and can put them to mending. They say the lady is fair:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ’tis a truth, I can bear them witness; and virtuous: ’tis so,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I cannot reprove it; and wise, but for loving me: by my troth, it is no

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: addition to her wit, nor no great argument of her folly, for I will be

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: horribly in love with her. I may chance have some odd quirks and remnants

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: of wit broken on me, because I have railed so long against marriage; but

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: doth not the appetite alter? A man loves the meat in his youth that he

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: cannot endure in his age. Shall quips and sentences and these paper

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: bullets of the brain awe a man from the career of his humour? No; the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: world must be peopled. When I said I would die a bachelor, I did not think

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I should live till I were married. Here comes Beatrice. By this day! she’s

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: a fair lady: I do spy some marks of love in her.
Enter Beatrice.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Against my will I am sent to bid you come in to dinner.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Fair Beatrice, I thank you for your pains.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I took no more pains for those thanks than you take pains to

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: thank me: if it had been painful, I would not have come.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: You take pleasure then in the message?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Yea, just so much as you may take upon a knife’s point,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and choke a daw withal. You have no stomach, signior: fare you well.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Ha! ‘Against my will I am sent to bid you come in to

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: dinner,’ there’s a double meaning in that. ‘I took no

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: more pains for those thanks than you took pains to thank me,’ that’s

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: as much as to say, Any pains that I take for you is as easy as thanks. If

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I do not take pity of her, I am a villain; if I do not love her, I am a

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Jew. I will go get her picture.
[Exit.]
Enter Hero, Margaret and Ursula.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Good Margaret, run thee to the parlour;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: There shalt thou find my cousin Beatrice

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Proposing with the Prince and Claudio:

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Whisper her ear, and tell her, I and Ursala

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Walk in the orchard, and our whole discourse

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Is all of her; say that thou overheard’st us,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And bid her steal into the pleached bower,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Where honey-suckles, ripen’d by the sun,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Forbid the sun to enter; like favourites,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Made proud by princes, that advance their pride

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Against that power that bred it. There will she hide her,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: To listen our propose. This is thy office;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Bear thee well in it and leave us alone.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: I’ll make her come, I warrant you, presently.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Now, Ursula, when Beatrice doth come,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: As we do trace this alley up and down,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Our talk must only be of Benedick:

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: When I do name him, let it be thy part

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: To praise him more than ever man did merit.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: My talk to thee must be how Benedick

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Is sick in love with Beatrice: of this matter

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Is little Cupid’s crafty arrow made,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: That only wounds by hearsay.
Enter Beatrice behind.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Now begin;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: For look where Beatrice, like a lapwing, runs

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Close by the ground, to hear our conference.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: The pleasant’st angling is to see the fish

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Cut with her golden oars the silver stream,

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: And greedily devour the treacherous bait:

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: So angle we for Beatrice; who even now

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Is couched in the woodbine coverture.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Fear you not my part of the dialogue.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Then go we near her, that her ear lose nothing

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Of the false sweet bait that we lay for it.
[They advance to the bower.]

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: No, truly, Ursula, she is too disdainful;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: I know her spirits are as coy and wild

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: As haggards of the rock.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: But are you sure

lines.speaker: URSULA
