lines.text: That Benedick loves Beatrice so entirely?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: So says the Prince, and my new-trothed lord.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: And did they bid you tell her of it, madam?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: They did entreat me to acquaint her of it;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: But I persuaded them, if they lov’d Benedick,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: To wish him wrestle with affection,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And never to let Beatrice know of it.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Why did you so? Doth not the gentleman

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Deserve as full as fortunate a bed

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: As ever Beatrice shall couch upon?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: O god of love! I know he doth deserve

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: As much as may be yielded to a man;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: But Nature never fram’d a woman’s heart

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Of prouder stuff than that of Beatrice;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Disdain and scorn ride sparkling in her eyes,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Misprising what they look on, and her wit

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Values itself so highly, that to her

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: All matter else seems weak. She cannot love,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Nor take no shape nor project of affection,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: She is so self-endear’d.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Sure I think so;

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: And therefore certainly it were not good

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: She knew his love, lest she make sport at it.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Why, you speak truth. I never yet saw man,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: How wise, how noble, young, how rarely featur’d,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: But she would spell him backward: if fair-fac’d,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: She would swear the gentleman should be her sister;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: If black, why, Nature, drawing of an antick,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Made a foul blot; if tall, a lance ill-headed;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: If low, an agate very vilely cut;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: If speaking, why, a vane blown with all winds;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: If silent, why, a block moved with none.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: So turns she every man the wrong side out,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And never gives to truth and virtue that

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Which simpleness and merit purchaseth.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Sure, sure, such carping is not commendable.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: No; not to be so odd, and from all fashions,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: As Beatrice is, cannot be commendable.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: But who dare tell her so? If I should speak,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: She would mock me into air: O! she would laugh me

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Out of myself, press me to death with wit.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Therefore let Benedick, like cover’d fire,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Consume away in sighs, waste inwardly:

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: It were a better death than die with mocks,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Which is as bad as die with tickling.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Yet tell her of it: hear what she will say.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: No; rather I will go to Benedick,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And counsel him to fight against his passion.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And, truly, I’ll devise some honest slanders

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: To stain my cousin with. One doth not know

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: How much an ill word may empoison liking.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: O! do not do your cousin such a wrong.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: She cannot be so much without true judgment,—

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Having so swift and excellent a wit

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: As she is priz’d to have,—as to refuse

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: So rare a gentleman as Signior Benedick.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: He is the only man of Italy,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Always excepted my dear Claudio.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: I pray you, be not angry with me, madam,

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Speaking my fancy: Signior Benedick,

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: For shape, for bearing, argument and valour,

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Goes foremost in report through Italy.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Indeed, he hath an excellent good name.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: His excellence did earn it, ere he had it.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: When are you married, madam?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Why, every day, tomorrow. Come, go in:

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: I’ll show thee some attires, and have thy counsel

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Which is the best to furnish me tomorrow.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: She’s lim’d, I warrant you,

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: We have caught her, madam.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: If it prove so, then loving goes by haps:

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Some Cupid kills with arrows, some with traps.
[Exeunt Hero and Ursula.]
[Advancing.]

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: What fire is in mine ears? Can this be true?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Stand I condemn’d for pride and scorn so much?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Contempt, farewell! and maiden pride, adieu!

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No glory lives behind the back of such.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: And, Benedick, love on; I will requite thee,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Taming my wild heart to thy loving hand:

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: If thou dost love, my kindness shall incite thee

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: To bind our loves up in a holy band;

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: For others say thou dost deserve, and I

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Believe it better than reportingly.
[Exit.]
Enter Don Pedro, Claudio, Benedick and Leonato.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I do but stay till your marriage be consummate, and then go I toward Arragon.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I’ll bring you thither, my lord, if you’ll

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: vouchsafe me.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Nay, that would be as great a soil in the new gloss of your

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: marriage, as to show a child his new coat and forbid him to wear it. I

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: will only be bold with Benedick for his company; for, from the crown of

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: his head to the sole of his foot, he is all mirth; he hath twice or thrice

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: cut Cupid’s bowstring, and the little hangman dare not shoot at him.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: He hath a heart as sound as a bell, and his tongue is the clapper; for

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: what his heart thinks, his tongue speaks.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Gallants, I am not as I have been.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: So say I: methinks you are sadder.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I hope he be in love.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Hang him, truant! there’s no true drop of blood in him

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: to be truly touched with love. If he be sad, he wants money.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I have the tooth-ache.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Draw it.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Hang it.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: You must hang it first, and draw it afterwards.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What! sigh for the tooth-ache?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Where is but a humour or a worm?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Well, everyone can master a grief but he that has it.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yet say I, he is in love.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: There is no appearance of fancy in him, unless it be a fancy

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: that he hath to strange disguises; as to be a Dutchman today, a Frenchman

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: tomorrow; or in the shape of two countries at once, as a German from the

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: waist downward, all slops, and a Spaniard from the hip upward, no doublet.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Unless he have a fancy to this foolery, as it appears he hath, he is no

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: fool for fancy, as you would have it appear he is.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If he be not in love with some woman, there is no believing old

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: signs: a’ brushes his hat a mornings; what should that bode?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Hath any man seen him at the barber’s?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: No, but the barber’s man hath been seen with him; and the

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: old ornament of his cheek hath already stuffed tennis balls.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Indeed he looks younger than he did, by the loss of a beard.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Nay, a’ rubs himself with civet: can you smell him out by that?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That’s as much as to say the sweet youth’s in love.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: The greatest note of it is his melancholy.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And when was he wont to wash his face?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Yea, or to paint himself? for the which, I hear what they say of him.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Nay, but his jesting spirit; which is now crept into a

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: lute-string, and now governed by stops.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Indeed, that tells a heavy tale for him. Conclude, conclude he is in love.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Nay, but I know who loves him.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: That would I know too: I warrant, one that knows him not.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yes, and his ill conditions; and in despite of all, dies for him.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: She shall be buried with her face upwards.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Yet is this no charm for the tooth-ache. Old signior, walk aside

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: with me: I have studied eight or nine wise words to speak to you, which

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: these hobby-horses must not hear.
[Exeunt Benedick and Leonato.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: For my life, to break with him about Beatrice.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: ’Tis even so. Hero and Margaret have by this played

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: their parts with Beatrice, and then the two bears will not bite one

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: another when they meet.
Enter Don John.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: My lord and brother, God save you!

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Good den, brother.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: If your leisure served, I would speak with you.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: In private?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: If it please you; yet Count Claudio may hear, for what I would

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: speak of concerns him.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What’s the matter?
[To Claudio.]

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Means your lordship to be married tomorrow?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: You know he does.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I know not that, when he knows what I know.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If there be any impediment, I pray you discover it.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: You may think I love you not: let that appear hereafter, and aim

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: better at me by that I now will manifest. For my brother, I think he holds

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: you well, and in dearness of heart hath holp to effect your ensuing

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: marriage; surely suit ill-spent and labour ill bestowed!

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Why, what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I came hither to tell you; and circumstances shortened,—for she

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: has been too long a talking of,—the lady is disloyal.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Who, Hero?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Even she: Leonato’s Hero, your Hero, every man’s Hero.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Disloyal?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: The word’s too good to paint out her wickedness; I could

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: say, she were worse: think you of a worse title, and I will fit her to it.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Wonder not till further warrant: go but with me tonight, you shall see

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: her chamber window entered, even the night before her wedding-day: if you

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: love her then, tomorrow wed her; but it would better fit your honour to

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: change your mind.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: May this be so?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I will not think it.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: If you dare not trust that you see, confess not that you know.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: If you will follow me, I will show you enough; and when you have seen more

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: and heard more, proceed accordingly.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If I see anything tonight why I should not marry her tomorrow,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: in the congregation, where I should wed, there will I shame her.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And, as I wooed for thee to obtain her, I will join with thee

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: to disgrace her.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I will disparage her no farther till you are my witnesses: bear

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: it coldly but till midnight, and let the issue show itself.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: O day untowardly turned!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O mischief strangely thwarting!

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: O plague right well prevented! So will you say when you have seen

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: the sequel.
[Exeunt.]

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Scene III. A Street.
Enter Dogberry and Verges, with the Watch.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Are you good men and true?

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Yea, or else it were pity but they should suffer salvation, body and soul.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Nay, that were a punishment too good for them, if they should

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: have any allegiance in them, being chosen for the Prince’s watch.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Well, give them their charge, neighbour Dogberry.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: First, who think you the most desartless man to be constable?

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: Hugh Oatcake, sir, or George Seacoal; for they can write and read.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Come hither, neighbour Seacoal. God hath blessed you with a good

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: name: to be a well-favoured man is the gift of Fortune; but to write and

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: read comes by Nature.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: Both which, Master Constable,—

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: You have: I knew it would be your answer. Well, for your favour,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: sir, why, give God thanks, and make no boast of it; and for your writing

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: and reading, let that appear when there is no need of such vanity. You are

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: thought here to be the most senseless and fit man for the constable of the

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: watch; therefore bear you the lanthorn. This is your charge: you shall

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: comprehend all vagrom men; you are to bid any man stand, in the Prince’s

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: name.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: How, if a’ will not stand?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Why, then, take no note of him, but let him go; and presently

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: call the rest of the watch together, and thank God you are rid of a knave.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: If he will not stand when he is bidden, he is none of the Prince’s

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: subjects.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: True, and they are to meddle with none but the Prince’s

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: subjects. You shall also make no noise in the streets: for, for the

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: watch to babble and to talk is most tolerable and not to be endured.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: We will rather sleep than talk: we know what belongs to a watch.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Why, you speak like an ancient and most quiet watchman, for I

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: cannot see how sleeping should offend; only have a care that your bills be

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: not stolen. Well, you are to call at all the alehouses, and bid those that

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: are drunk get them to bed.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: How if they will not?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Why then, let them alone till they are sober: if they make you

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: not then the better answer, you may say they are not the men you took them

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: for.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: Well, sir.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: If you meet a thief, you may suspect him, by virtue of your

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: office, to be no true man; and, for such kind of men, the less you meddle

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: or make with them, why, the more is for your honesty.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: If we know him to be a thief, shall we not lay hands on him?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Truly, by your office, you may; but I think they that touch

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: pitch will be defiled. The most peaceable way for you, if you do take a

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: thief, is to let him show himself what he is and steal out of your

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: company.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: You have been always called a merciful man, partner.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Truly, I would not hang a dog by my will, much more a man who

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: hath any honesty in him.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: If you hear a child cry in the night, you must call to the nurse

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: and bid her still it.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: How if the nurse be asleep and will not hear us?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Why then, depart in peace, and let the child wake her with

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: crying; for the ewe that will not hear her lamb when it baes, will never

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: answer a calf when he bleats.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: ’Tis very true.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: This is the end of the charge. You constable, are to present the

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Prince’s own person: if you meet the Prince in the night, you may

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: stay him.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Nay, by’r lady, that I think, a’ cannot.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Five shillings to one on’t, with any man that knows the

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: statutes, he may stay him: marry, not without the Prince be willing; for,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: indeed, the watch ought to offend no man, and it is an offence to stay a

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: man against his will.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: By’r lady, I think it be so.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Ha, ah, ha! Well, masters, good night: an there be any matter of

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: weight chances, call up me: keep your fellows’ counsels and your

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: own, and good night. Come, neighbour.

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: Well, masters, we hear our charge: let us go sit here upon

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: the church bench till two, and then all to bed.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: One word more, honest neighbours. I pray you, watch about

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Signior Leonato’s door; for the wedding being there tomorrow,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: there is a great coil tonight. Adieu; be vigitant, I beseech

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: you.
[Exeunt Dogberry and Verges.]
Enter Borachio and Conrade.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: What, Conrade!
[Aside]

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: Peace! stir not.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Conrade, I say!

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Here, man. I am at thy elbow.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Mass, and my elbow itched; I thought there would a scab follow.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: I will owe thee an answer for that; and now forward with thy tale.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Stand thee close then under this penthouse, for it drizzles

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: rain, and I will, like a true drunkard, utter all to thee.
[Aside]

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: Some treason, masters; yet stand close.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Therefore know, I have earned of Don John a thousand ducats.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Is it possible that any villainy should be so dear?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Thou shouldst rather ask if it were possible any villainy should

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: be so rich; for when rich villains have need of poor ones, poor ones may

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: make what price they will.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: I wonder at it.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: That shows thou art unconfirmed. Thou knowest that the fashion

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: of a doublet, or a hat, or a cloak, is nothing to a man.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Yes, it is apparel.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: I mean, the fashion.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Yes, the fashion is the fashion.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Tush! I may as well say the fool’s the fool. But seest

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: thou not what a deformed thief this fashion is?
[Aside]

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: I know that Deformed; a’ has been a vile thief

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: this seven years; a’ goes up and down like a gentleman: I remember

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: his name.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Didst thou not hear somebody?

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: No: ’twas the vane on the house.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Seest thou not, I say, what a deformed thief this fashion is?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: how giddily he turns about all the hot bloods between fourteen and

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: five-and-thirty? sometime fashioning them like Pharaoh’s soldiers in

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: the reechy painting; sometime like god Bel’s priests in the old

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: church window; sometime like the shaven Hercules in the smirched

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: worm-eaten tapestry, where his codpiece seems as massy as his club?

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: All this I see, and I see that the fashion wears out more apparel

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: than the man. But art not thou thyself giddy with the fashion too, that

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: thou hast shifted out of thy tale into telling me of the fashion?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Not so neither; but know, that I have tonight wooed Margaret,

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: the Lady Hero’s gentlewoman, by the name of Hero: she leans me out

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: at her mistress’ chamber window, bids me a thousand times good

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: night,—I tell this tale vilely:—I should first tell thee how the Prince,

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Claudio, and my master, planted and placed and possessed by my master Don

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: John, saw afar off in the orchard this amiable encounter.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: And thought they Margaret was Hero?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Two of them did, the Prince and Claudio; but the devil my

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: master, knew she was Margaret; and partly by his oaths, which first

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: possessed them, partly by the dark night, which did deceive them, but

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: chiefly by my villainy, which did confirm any slander that Don John had

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: made, away went Claudio enraged; swore he would meet her, as he was

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: appointed, next morning at the temple, and there, before the whole

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: congregation, shame her with what he saw o’er night, and send her

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: home again without a husband.

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: We charge you in the Prince’s name, stand!

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: Call up the right Master Constable. We have here recovered

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: the most dangerous piece of lechery that ever was known in the

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: commonwealth.

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: And one Deformed is one of them: I know him, a’ wears a lock.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Masters, masters!

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: You’ll be made bring Deformed forth, I warrant you.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Masters,—

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: Never speak: we charge you let us obey you to go with us.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: We are like to prove a goodly commodity, being taken up of these

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: men’s bills.

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: A commodity in question, I warrant you. Come, we’ll obey you.
[Exeunt.]

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Scene IV. A Room in Leonato’s House.
Enter Hero, Margaret and Ursula.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Good Ursula, wake my cousin Beatrice, and desire her to rise.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: I will, lady.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And bid her come hither.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Well.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Troth, I think your other rebato were better.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: No, pray thee, good Meg, I’ll wear this.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: By my troth’s not so good; and I warrant your cousin will say so.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: My cousin’s a fool, and thou art another: I’ll

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: wear none but this.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: I like the new tire within excellently, if the hair were a thought

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: browner; and your gown’s a most rare fashion, i’ faith. I saw the

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Duchess of Milan’s gown that they praise so.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: O! that exceeds, they say.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: By my troth ’s but a night-gown in respect of yours: cloth o’ gold, and

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: cuts, and laced with silver, set with pearls, down sleeves, side

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: sleeves, and skirts round, underborne with a bluish tinsel; but for a

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: fine, quaint, graceful, and excellent fashion, yours is worth ten on’t.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: God give me joy to wear it! for my heart is exceeding heavy.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: ’Twill be heavier soon by the weight of a man.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Fie upon thee! art not ashamed?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Of what, lady? of speaking honourably? Is not marriage honourable in a

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: beggar? Is not your lord honourable without marriage? I think you would

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: have me say, saving your reverence, ‘a husband:’ an bad thinking do not

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: wrest true speaking, I’ll offend nobody. Is there any harm in ‘the

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: heavier for a husband’? None, I think, and it be the right husband and

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: the right wife; otherwise ’tis light, and not heavy: ask my Lady

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Beatrice else; here she comes.
Enter Beatrice.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Good morrow, coz.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Good morrow, sweet Hero.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Why, how now? do you speak in the sick tune?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I am out of all other tune, methinks.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Clap’s into ‘Light o’ love’; that goes

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: without a burden: do you sing it, and I’ll dance it.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Ye, light o’ love with your heels! then, if your husband

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: have stables enough, you’ll see he shall lack no barnes.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: O illegitimate construction! I scorn that with my heels.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: ’Tis almost five o’clock, cousin; ’tis time

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: you were ready. By my troth, I am exceeding ill. Heigh-ho!

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: For a hawk, a horse, or a husband?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: For the letter that begins them all, H.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Well, and you be not turned Turk, there’s no more

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: sailing by the star.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: What means the fool, trow?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Nothing I; but God send everyone their heart’s desire!

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: These gloves the Count sent me; they are an excellent perfume.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I am stuffed, cousin, I cannot smell.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: A maid, and stuffed! there’s goodly catching of cold.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: O, God help me! God help me! how long have you professed

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: apprehension?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Ever since you left it. Doth not my wit become me rarely!

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: It is not seen enough, you should wear it in your cap. By

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: my troth, I am sick.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Get you some of this distilled Carduus benedictus, and lay it to

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: your heart: it is the only thing for a qualm.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: There thou prick’st her with a thistle.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Benedictus! why benedictus? you have some moral in this

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: benedictus.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Moral! no, by my troth, I have no moral meaning; I meant, plain

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: holy thistle. You may think, perchance, that I think you are in love: nay,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: by’r Lady, I am not such a fool to think what I list; nor I list not

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: to think what I can; nor, indeed, I cannot think, if I would think my

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: heart out of thinking, that you are in love, or that you will be in love,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: or that you can be in love. Yet Benedick was such another, and now is he

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: become a man: he swore he would never marry; and yet now, in despite of

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: his heart, he eats his meat without grudging: and how you may be

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: converted, I know not; but methinks you look with your eyes as other women

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: do.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: What pace is this that thy tongue keeps?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Not a false gallop.
Re-enter Ursula.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Madam, withdraw: the Prince, the Count, Signior Benedick, Don

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: John, and all the gallants of the town are come to fetch you to church.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Help to dress me, good coz, good Meg, good Ursula.
[Exeunt.]

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Scene V. Another Room in Leonato’s House.
Enter Leonato and Dogberry and Verges.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What would you with me, honest neighbour?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Marry, sir, I would have some confidence with you, that decerns

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: you nearly.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Brief, I pray you; for you see it is a busy time with me.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Marry, this it is, sir.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Yes, in truth it is, sir.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What is it, my good friends?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Goodman Verges, sir, speaks a little off the matter: an old man,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: sir, and his wits are not so blunt as, God help, I would desire they were;

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: but, in faith, honest as the skin between his brows.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Yes, I thank God, I am as honest as any man living, that is an old

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: man and no honester than I.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Comparisons are odorous: palabras, neighbour Verges.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Neighbours, you are tedious.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: It pleases your worship to say so, but we are the poor Duke’s

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: officers; but truly, for mine own part, if I were as tedious as a king, I

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: could find in my heart to bestow it all of your worship.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: All thy tediousness on me! ah?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Yea, and ’twere a thousand pound more than ’tis;

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: for I hear as good exclamation on your worship, as of any man in the

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: city, and though I be but a poor man, I am glad to hear it.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: And so am I.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I would fain know what you have to say.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Marry, sir, our watch tonight, excepting your worship’s

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: presence, ha’ ta’en a couple of as arrant knaves as any in

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Messina.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: A good old man, sir; he will be talking; as they say, ‘when

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: the age is in, the wit is out.’ God help us! it is a world to see!

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Well said, i’ faith, neighbour Verges: well, God’s a good man;

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: and two men ride of a horse, one must ride behind. An honest soul, i’

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: faith, sir; by my troth he is, as ever broke bread; but God is to be

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: worshipped: all men are not alike; alas! good neighbour.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Indeed, neighbour, he comes too short of you.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Gifts that God gives.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I must leave you.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: One word, sir: our watch, sir, have indeed comprehended two

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: aspicious persons, and we would have them this morning examined before

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: your worship.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Take their examination yourself, and bring it me: I am now in

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: great haste, as may appear unto you.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: It shall be suffigance.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Drink some wine ere you go: fare you well.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, they stay for you to give your daughter to her husband.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I’ll wait upon them: I am ready.
[Exeunt Leonato and Messenger.]

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Go, good partner, go get you to Francis Seacoal; bid him bring

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: his pen and inkhorn to the gaol: we are now to examination these men.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: And we must do it wisely.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: We will spare for no wit, I warrant you; here’s that shall

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: drive some of them to a non-come: only get the learned writer to set down

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: our excommunication, and meet me at the gaol.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Don Pedro, Don John, Leonato, Friar Francis, Claudio, Benedick, Hero, Beatrice &c.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Come, Friar Francis, be brief: only to the plain form of

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: marriage, and you shall recount their particular duties afterwards.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: You come hither, my lord, to marry this lady?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: To be married to her, friar; you come to marry her.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Lady, you come hither to be married to this Count?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: If either of you know any inward impediment, why you should not be

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: conjoined, I charge you, on your souls, to utter it.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Know you any, Hero?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: None, my lord.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Know you any, Count?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I dare make his answer; none.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O! what men dare do! what men may do! what men daily do, not

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: knowing what they do!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: How now! Interjections? Why then, some be of laughing, as ah!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ha! he!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Stand thee by, Friar. Father, by your leave:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Will you with free and unconstrained soul

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Give me this maid, your daughter?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: As freely, son, as God did give her me.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And what have I to give you back whose worth

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: May counterpoise this rich and precious gift?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Nothing, unless you render her again.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Sweet Prince, you learn me noble thankfulness.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: There, Leonato, take her back again:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Give not this rotten orange to your friend;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: She’s but the sign and semblance of her honour.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Behold! how like a maid she blushes here.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O! what authority and show of truth

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Can cunning sin cover itself withal.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Comes not that blood as modest evidence

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: To witness simple virtue? Would you not swear,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: All you that see her, that she were a maid,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: By these exterior shows? But she is none:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: She knows the heat of a luxurious bed;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Her blush is guiltiness, not modesty.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What do you mean, my lord?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Not to be married,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Not to knit my soul to an approved wanton.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Dear my lord, if you, in your own proof,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Have vanquish’d the resistance of her youth,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And made defeat of her virginity,—

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I know what you would say: if I have known her,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: You will say she did embrace me as a husband,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And so extenuate the forehand sin: No, Leonato,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I never tempted her with word too large;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But as a brother to his sister show’d

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Bashful sincerity and comely love.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And seem’d I ever otherwise to you?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Out on thee! Seeming! I will write against it:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: You seem to me as Dian in her orb,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: As chaste as is the bud ere it be blown;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But you are more intemperate in your blood

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Than Venus, or those pamper’d animals

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That rage in savage sensuality.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Is my lord well, that he doth speak so wide?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Sweet Prince, why speak not you?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What should I speak?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I stand dishonour’d, that have gone about

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: To link my dear friend to a common stale.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Are these things spoken, or do I but dream?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Sir, they are spoken, and these things are true.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: This looks not like a nuptial.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: True! O God!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Leonato, stand I here?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Is this the Prince? Is this the Prince’s brother?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Is this face Hero’s? Are our eyes our own?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: All this is so; but what of this, my lord?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Let me but move one question to your daughter,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And by that fatherly and kindly power

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: That you have in her, bid her answer truly.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I charge thee do so, as thou art my child.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: O, God defend me! how am I beset!

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: What kind of catechizing call you this?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: To make you answer truly to your name.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Is it not Hero? Who can blot that name

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: With any just reproach?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Marry, that can Hero:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Hero itself can blot out Hero’s virtue.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: What man was he talk’d with you yesternight

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Out at your window, betwixt twelve and one?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Now, if you are a maid, answer to this.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: I talk’d with no man at that hour, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Why, then are you no maiden.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Leonato, I am sorry you must hear: upon my honour,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Myself, my brother, and this grieved Count,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Did see her, hear her, at that hour last night,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Talk with a ruffian at her chamber window;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Who hath indeed, most like a liberal villain,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Confess’d the vile encounters they have had

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: A thousand times in secret.

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Fie, fie! they are not to be nam’d, my lord,

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Not to be spoke of;

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: There is not chastity enough in language

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Without offence to utter them. Thus, pretty lady,

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: I am sorry for thy much misgovernment.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O Hero! what a Hero hadst thou been,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If half thy outward graces had been plac’d

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: About thy thoughts and counsels of thy heart!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But fare thee well, most foul, most fair! farewell,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Thou pure impiety, and impious purity!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: For thee I’ll lock up all the gates of love,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And on my eyelids shall conjecture hang,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: To turn all beauty into thoughts of harm,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And never shall it more be gracious.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Hath no man’s dagger here a point for me?
[Hero swoons.]

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Why, how now, cousin! wherefore sink you down?

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Come, let us go. These things, come thus to light,

lines.speaker: DON JOHN
lines.text: Smother her spirits up.
[Exeunt Don Pedro, Don John and Claudio.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: How doth the lady?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Dead, I think! Help, uncle! Hero! why, Hero! Uncle! Signior

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Benedick! Friar!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O Fate! take not away thy heavy hand:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Death is the fairest cover for her shame

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That may be wish’d for.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: How now, cousin Hero?

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Have comfort, lady.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Dost thou look up?

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Yea; wherefore should she not?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Wherefore! Why, doth not every earthly thing

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Cry shame upon her? Could she here deny

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The story that is printed in her blood?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Do not live, Hero; do not ope thine eyes;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: For, did I think thou wouldst not quickly die,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Thought I thy spirits were stronger than thy shames,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Myself would, on the rearward of reproaches,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Strike at thy life. Griev’d I, I had but one?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Chid I for that at frugal Nature’s frame?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O! one too much by thee. Why had I one?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Why ever wast thou lovely in my eyes?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Why had I not with charitable hand

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Took up a beggar’s issue at my gates,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Who smirched thus, and mir’d with infamy,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I might have said, ‘No part of it is mine;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: This shame derives itself from unknown loins?’

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But mine, and mine I lov’d, and mine I prais’d,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And mine that I was proud on, mine so much

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That I myself was to myself not mine,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Valuing of her; why, she—O! she is fallen

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Into a pit of ink, that the wide sea

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Hath drops too few to wash her clean again,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And salt too little which may season give

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: To her foul tainted flesh.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Sir, sir, be patient.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: For my part, I am so attir’d in wonder,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I know not what to say.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: O! on my soul, my cousin is belied!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Lady, were you her bedfellow last night?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No, truly, not; although, until last night,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I have this twelvemonth been her bedfellow.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Confirm’d, confirm’d! O! that is stronger made,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Which was before barr’d up with ribs of iron.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Would the two princes lie? and Claudio lie,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Who lov’d her so, that, speaking of her foulness,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Wash’d it with tears? Hence from her! let her die.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Hear me a little;

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: For I have only been silent so long,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And given way unto this course of fortune,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: By noting of the lady: I have mark’d

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: A thousand blushing apparitions

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: To start into her face; a thousand innocent shames

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: In angel whiteness bear away those blushes;

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And in her eye there hath appear’d a fire,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: To burn the errors that these princes hold

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Against her maiden truth. Call me a fool;

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Trust not my reading nor my observations,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Which with experimental seal doth warrant

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: The tenure of my book; trust not my age,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: My reverence, calling, nor divinity,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: If this sweet lady lie not guiltless here

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Under some biting error.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Friar, it cannot be.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Thou seest that all the grace that she hath left

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Is that she will not add to her damnation

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: A sin of perjury: she not denies it.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Why seek’st thou then to cover with excuse

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That which appears in proper nakedness?

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Lady, what man is he you are accus’d of?

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: They know that do accuse me, I know none;

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: If I know more of any man alive

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Than that which maiden modesty doth warrant,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Let all my sins lack mercy! O, my father!

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Prove you that any man with me convers’d

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: At hours unmeet, or that I yesternight

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Maintain’d the change of words with any creature,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Refuse me, hate me, torture me to death.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: There is some strange misprision in the princes.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Two of them have the very bent of honour;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And if their wisdoms be misled in this,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: The practice of it lives in John the bastard,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Whose spirits toil in frame of villainies.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I know not. If they speak but truth of her,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: These hands shall tear her; if they wrong her honour,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The proudest of them shall well hear of it.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Time hath not yet so dried this blood of mine,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Nor age so eat up my invention,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Nor fortune made such havoc of my means,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Nor my bad life reft me so much of friends,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But they shall find, awak’d in such a kind,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Both strength of limb and policy of mind,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Ability in means and choice of friends,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: To quit me of them throughly.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Pause awhile,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And let my counsel sway you in this case.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Your daughter here the princes left for dead;

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Let her awhile be secretly kept in,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And publish it that she is dead indeed:

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Maintain a mourning ostentation;

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And on your family’s old monument

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Hang mournful epitaphs and do all rites

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: That appertain unto a burial.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What shall become of this? What will this do?

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Marry, this well carried shall on her behalf

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Change slander to remorse; that is some good.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: But not for that dream I on this strange course,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: But on this travail look for greater birth.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: She dying, as it must be so maintain’d,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Upon the instant that she was accus’d,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Shall be lamented, pitied and excus’d

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Of every hearer; for it so falls out

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: That what we have we prize not to the worth

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Whiles we enjoy it, but being lack’d and lost,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Why, then we rack the value, then we find

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: The virtue that possession would not show us

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Whiles it was ours. So will it fare with Claudio:

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: When he shall hear she died upon his words,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: The idea of her life shall sweetly creep

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Into his study of imagination,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And every lovely organ of her life

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Shall come apparell’d in more precious habit,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: More moving, delicate, and full of life

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Into the eye and prospect of his soul,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Than when she liv’d indeed: then shall he mourn,—

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: If ever love had interest in his liver,—

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And wish he had not so accused her,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: No, though he thought his accusation true.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Let this be so, and doubt not but success

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Will fashion the event in better shape

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Than I can lay it down in likelihood.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: But if all aim but this be levell’d false,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: The supposition of the lady’s death

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Will quench the wonder of her infamy:

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And if it sort not well, you may conceal her,—

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: As best befits her wounded reputation,—

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: In some reclusive and religious life,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Out of all eyes, tongues, minds, and injuries.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Signior Leonato, let the friar advise you:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And though you know my inwardness and love

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Is very much unto the Prince and Claudio,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Yet, by mine honour, I will deal in this

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: As secretly and justly as your soul

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Should with your body.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Being that I flow in grief,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The smallest twine may lead me.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: ’Tis well consented: presently away;

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: For to strange sores strangely they strain the cure.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Come, lady, die to live: this wedding day

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Perhaps is but prolong’d: have patience and endure.
[Exeunt Friar, Hero and Leonato.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Lady Beatrice, have you wept all this while?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Yea, and I will weep a while longer.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I will not desire that.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: You have no reason; I do it freely.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Surely I do believe your fair cousin is wronged.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Ah! how much might the man deserve of me that would right her.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Is there any way to show such friendship?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: A very even way, but no such friend.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: May a man do it?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: It is a man’s office, but not yours.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I do love nothing in the world so well as you: is not that strange?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: As strange as the thing I know not. It were as possible for

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: me to say I loved nothing so well as you; but believe me not, and yet

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I lie not; I confess nothing, nor I deny nothing. I am sorry for my

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: cousin.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: By my sword, Beatrice, thou lovest me.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Do not swear by it, and eat it.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I will swear by it that you love me; and I will make him eat it

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: that says I love not you.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Will you not eat your word?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: With no sauce that can be devised to it. I protest I love thee.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Why then, God forgive me!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: What offence, sweet Beatrice?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: You have stayed me in a happy hour: I was about to protest I loved you.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And do it with all thy heart.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I love you with so much of my heart that none is left to protest.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Come, bid me do anything for thee.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Kill Claudio.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Ha! not for the wide world.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: You kill me to deny it. Farewell.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Tarry, sweet Beatrice.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I am gone, though I am here: there is no love in you: nay, I

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: pray you, let me go.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Beatrice,—

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: In faith, I will go.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: We’ll be friends first.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: You dare easier be friends with me than fight with mine enemy.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Is Claudio thine enemy?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Is he not approved in the height a villain, that hath slandered,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: scorned, dishonoured my kinswoman? O! that I were a man. What! bear her in

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: hand until they come to take hands, and then, with public accusation,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: uncovered slander, unmitigated rancour,—O God, that I were a man! I would

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: eat his heart in the market-place.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Hear me, Beatrice,—

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Talk with a man out at a window! a proper saying!

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Nay, but Beatrice,—

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Sweet Hero! she is wronged, she is slandered, she is undone.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Beat—

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Princes and Counties! Surely, a princely testimony, a goodly

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Count Comfect; a sweet gallant, surely! O! that I were a man for his sake,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: or that I had any friend would be a man for my sake! But manhood is melted

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: into curtsies, valour into compliment, and men are only turned into tongue,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and trim ones too: he is now as valiant as Hercules, that only tells a lie

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and swears it. I cannot be a man with wishing, therefore I will die a

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: woman with grieving.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Tarry, good Beatrice. By this hand, I love thee.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Use it for my love some other way than swearing by it.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Think you in your soul the Count Claudio hath wronged Hero?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Yea, as sure is I have a thought or a soul.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Enough! I am engaged, I will challenge him. I will kiss your

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: hand, and so leave you. By this hand, Claudio shall render me a dear

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: account. As you hear of me, so think of me. Go, comfort your cousin: I

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: must say she is dead; and so, farewell.
[Exeunt.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Scene II. A Prison.
Enter Dogberry, Verges, and Sexton, in gowns; and the Watch, with Conrade and Borachio.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Is our whole dissembly appeared?

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: O! a stool and a cushion for the sexton.

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: Which be the malefactors?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Marry, that am I and my partner.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Nay, that’s certain: we have the exhibition to examine.

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: But which are the offenders that are to be examined? let them come

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: before Master Constable.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Yea, marry, let them come before me. What is your name, friend?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Borachio.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Pray write down Borachio. Yours, sirrah?

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: I am a gentleman, sir, and my name is Conrade.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Write down Master gentleman Conrade. Masters, do you serve God?

lines.speaker: BOTH
lines.text: Yea, sir, we hope.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Write down that they hope they serve God: and write God first;

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: for God defend but God should go before such villains! Masters, it is

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: proved already that you are little better than false knaves, and it will

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: go near to be thought so shortly. How answer you for yourselves?

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Marry, sir, we say we are none.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: A marvellous witty fellow, I assure you; but I will go

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: about with him. Come you hither, sirrah; a word in your ear: sir, I

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: say to you, it is thought you are false knaves.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Sir, I say to you we are none.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Well, stand aside. Fore God, they are both in a tale. Have you

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: writ down, that they are none?

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: Master Constable, you go not the way to examine: you must call

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: forth the watch that are their accusers.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Yea, marry, that’s the eftest way. Let the watch come forth.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Masters, I charge you, in the Prince’s name, accuse these men.

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: This man said, sir, that Don John, the Prince’s

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: brother, was a villain.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Write down Prince John a villain. Why, this is flat perjury, to

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: call a Prince’s brother villain.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Master Constable,—

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Pray thee, fellow, peace: I do not like thy look, I promise thee.

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: What heard you him say else?

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: Marry, that he had received a thousand ducats of Don John

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: for accusing the Lady Hero wrongfully.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Flat burglary as ever was committed.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Yea, by the mass, that it is.

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: What else, fellow?

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: And that Count Claudio did mean, upon his words, to disgrace

lines.speaker: FIRST WATCH
lines.text: Hero before the whole assembly, and not marry her.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: O villain! thou wilt be condemned into everlasting redemption

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: for this.

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: What else?

lines.speaker: SECOND WATCH
lines.text: This is all.

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: And this is more, masters, than you can deny. Prince John is this

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: morning secretly stolen away: Hero was in this manner accused, in this

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: manner refused, and, upon the grief of this, suddenly died. Master

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: Constable, let these men be bound, and brought to Leonato’s: I will

lines.speaker: SEXTON
lines.text: go before and show him their examination.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Come, let them be opinioned.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Let them be in the hands—

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Off, coxcomb!

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: God’s my life! where’s the sexton? let him write

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: down the Prince’s officer coxcomb. Come, bind them. Thou naughty

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: varlet!

lines.speaker: CONRADE
lines.text: Away! you are an ass; you are an ass.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Dost thou not suspect my place? Dost thou not suspect my years?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: O that he were here to write me down an ass! but, masters, remember that I

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: am an ass; though it be not written down, yet forget not that I am an ass.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: No, thou villain, thou art full of piety, as shall be proved upon thee by

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: good witness. I am a wise fellow; and, which is more, an officer; and,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: which is more, a householder; and, which is more, as pretty a piece of

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: flesh as any in Messina; and one that knows the law, go to; and a rich

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: fellow enough, go to; and a fellow that hath had losses; and one that hath

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: two gowns, and everything handsome about him. Bring him away. O that I had

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: been writ down an ass!
[Exeunt.]
Enter Leonato and Antonio.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: If you go on thus, you will kill yourself

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And ’tis not wisdom thus to second grief

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Against yourself.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I pray thee, cease thy counsel,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Which falls into mine ears as profitless

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: As water in a sieve: give not me counsel;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Nor let no comforter delight mine ear

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But such a one whose wrongs do suit with mine:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Bring me a father that so lov’d his child,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Whose joy of her is overwhelm’d like mine,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And bid him speak of patience;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Measure his woe the length and breadth of mine,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And let it answer every strain for strain,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: As thus for thus and such a grief for such,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: In every lineament, branch, shape, and form:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: If such a one will smile, and stroke his beard;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Bid sorrow wag, cry ‘hem’ when he should groan,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Patch grief with proverbs; make misfortune drunk

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: With candle-wasters; bring him yet to me,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And I of him will gather patience.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But there is no such man; for, brother, men

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Can counsel and speak comfort to that grief

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Which they themselves not feel; but, tasting it,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Their counsel turns to passion, which before

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Would give preceptial medicine to rage,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Fetter strong madness in a silken thread,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Charm ache with air and agony with words.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No, no; ’tis all men’s office to speak patience

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: To those that wring under the load of sorrow,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But no man’s virtue nor sufficiency

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: To be so moral when he shall endure

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The like himself. Therefore give me no counsel:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My griefs cry louder than advertisement.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Therein do men from children nothing differ.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I pray thee peace! I will be flesh and blood;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: For there was never yet philosopher

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That could endure the toothache patiently,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: However they have writ the style of gods

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And made a push at chance and sufferance.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Yet bend not all the harm upon yourself;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Make those that do offend you suffer too.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: There thou speak’st reason: nay, I will do so.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My soul doth tell me Hero is belied;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And that shall Claudio know; so shall the Prince,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And all of them that thus dishonour her.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Here comes the Prince and Claudio hastily.
Enter Don Pedro and Claudio.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Good den, good den.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Good day to both of you.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Hear you, my lords,—

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: We have some haste, Leonato.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Some haste, my lord! well, fare you well, my lord:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Are you so hasty now?—well, all is one.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Nay, do not quarrel with us, good old man.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: If he could right himself with quarrelling,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Some of us would lie low.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Who wrongs him?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Marry, thou dost wrong me; thou dissembler, thou.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Nay, never lay thy hand upon thy sword;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I fear thee not.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Marry, beshrew my hand,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If it should give your age such cause of fear.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: In faith, my hand meant nothing to my sword.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Tush, tush, man! never fleer and jest at me:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I speak not like a dotard nor a fool,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: As, under privilege of age, to brag

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: What I have done being young, or what would do,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Were I not old. Know, Claudio, to thy head,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Thou hast so wrong’d mine innocent child and me

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That I am forc’d to lay my reverence by,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And, with grey hairs and bruise of many days,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Do challenge thee to trial of a man.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I say thou hast belied mine innocent child:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Thy slander hath gone through and through her heart,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And she lies buried with her ancestors;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: O! in a tomb where never scandal slept,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Save this of hers, fram’d by thy villainy!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: My villainy?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Thine, Claudio; thine, I say.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: You say not right, old man.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My lord, my lord,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I’ll prove it on his body, if he dare,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Despite his nice fence and his active practice,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: His May of youth and bloom of lustihood.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Away! I will not have to do with you.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Canst thou so daff me? Thou hast kill’d my child;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: If thou kill’st me, boy, thou shalt kill a man.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: He shall kill two of us, and men indeed:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: But that’s no matter; let him kill one first:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Win me and wear me; let him answer me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Come, follow me, boy; come, sir boy, come, follow me.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Sir boy, I’ll whip you from your foining fence;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Nay, as I am a gentleman, I will.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Brother,—

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Content yourself. God knows I lov’d my niece;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And she is dead, slander’d to death by villains,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That dare as well answer a man indeed

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: As I dare take a serpent by the tongue.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Boys, apes, braggarts, Jacks, milksops!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Brother Anthony,—

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Hold you content. What, man! I know them, yea,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And what they weigh, even to the utmost scruple,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Scambling, out-facing, fashion-monging boys,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: That lie and cog and flout, deprave and slander,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Go antickly, show outward hideousness,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And speak off half a dozen dangerous words,

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: How they might hurt their enemies, if they durst;

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And this is all!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But, brother Anthony,—

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Come, ’tis no matter:

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Do not you meddle, let me deal in this.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Gentlemen both, we will not wake your patience.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: My heart is sorry for your daughter’s death;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: But, on my honour, she was charg’d with nothing

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: But what was true and very full of proof.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My lord, my lord—

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I will not hear you.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No? Come, brother, away. I will be heard.—

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: And shall, or some of us will smart for it.
[Exeunt Leonato and Antonio.]
Enter Benedick.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: See, see; here comes the man we went to seek.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Now, signior, what news?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Good day, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Welcome, signior: you are almost come to part almost a fray.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: We had like to have had our two noses snapped off with two old

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: men without teeth.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Leonato and his brother. What think’st thou? Had we

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: fought, I doubt we should have been too young for them.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: In a false quarrel there is no true valour. I came to seek you both.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: We have been up and down to seek thee; for we are high-proof

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: melancholy, and would fain have it beaten away. Wilt thou use thy wit?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: It is in my scabbard; shall I draw it?

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Dost thou wear thy wit by thy side?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Never any did so, though very many have been beside their wit. I

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: will bid thee draw, as we do the minstrels; draw, to pleasure us.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: As I am an honest man, he looks pale. Art thou sick, or angry?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: What, courage, man! What though care killed a cat, thou hast

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: mettle enough in thee to kill care.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Sir, I shall meet your wit in the career, and you charge it

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: against me. I pray you choose another subject.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Nay then, give him another staff: this last was broke cross.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: By this light, he changes more and more: I think he be angry indeed.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: If he be, he knows how to turn his girdle.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Shall I speak a word in your ear?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: God bless me from a challenge!
[Aside to Claudio.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: You are a villain, I jest not: I will

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: make it good how you dare, with what you dare, and when you dare. Do me

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: right, or I will protest your cowardice. You have killed a sweet lady, and

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: her death shall fall heavy on you. Let me hear from you.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Well I will meet you, so I may have good cheer.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
