lines.text: What, a feast, a feast?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I’ faith, I thank him; he hath bid me to a calf’s-head

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: and a capon, the which if I do not carve most curiously, say my knife’s

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: naught. Shall I not find a woodcock too?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Sir, your wit ambles well; it goes easily.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I’ll tell thee how Beatrice praised thy wit the

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: other day. I said, thou hadst a fine wit. ‘True,’ says

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: she, ‘a fine little one.’ ‘No,’ said I,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: ‘a great wit.’ ‘Right,’ said she, ‘a

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: great gross one.’ ‘Nay,’ said I, ‘a good wit.’

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: ‘Just,’ said she, ‘it hurts nobody.’ ‘Nay,’

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: said I, ‘the gentleman is wise.’ ‘Certain,’

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: said she, ‘a wise gentleman.’ ‘Nay,’ said I,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: ‘he hath the tongues.’ ‘That I believe’ said

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: she, ‘for he swore a thing to me on Monday night, which he

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: forswore on Tuesday morning: there’s a double tongue; there’s

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: two tongues.’ Thus did she, an hour together, trans-shape thy

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: particular virtues; yet at last she concluded with a sigh, thou wast

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: the properest man in Italy.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: For the which she wept heartily and said she cared not.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Yea, that she did; but yet, for all that, an if she did not

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: hate him deadly, she would love him dearly. The old man’s daughter

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: told us all.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: All, all; and moreover, God saw him when he was hid in the garden.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: But when shall we set the savage bull’s horns on the

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: sensible Benedick’s head?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yea, and text underneath, ‘Here dwells Benedick the

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: married man!’

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Fare you well, boy: you know my mind. I will leave you now to

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: your gossip-like humour; you break jests as braggarts do their blades,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: which, God be thanked, hurt not. My lord, for your many courtesies I thank

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: you: I must discontinue your company. Your brother the bastard is fled

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: from Messina: you have, among you, killed a sweet and innocent lady. For

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: my Lord Lack-beard there, he and I shall meet; and till then, peace be

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: with him.
[Exit.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: He is in earnest.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: In most profound earnest; and, I’ll warrant you, for

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: the love of Beatrice.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And hath challenged thee?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Most sincerely.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What a pretty thing man is when he goes in his doublet and hose

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: and leaves off his wit!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: He is then a giant to an ape; but then is an ape a doctor to such

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: a man.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: But, soft you; let me be: pluck up, my heart, and be sad! Did

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: he not say my brother was fled?
Enter Dogberry, Verges,  and the Watch, with Conrade and Borachio.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Come you, sir: if justice cannot tame you, she shall ne’er

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: weigh more reasons in her balance. Nay, an you be a cursing hypocrite

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: once, you must be looked to.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: How now! two of my brother’s men bound! Borachio, one!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Hearken after their offence, my lord.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Officers, what offence have these men done?

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Marry, sir, they have committed false report; moreover, they

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: have spoken untruths; secondarily, they are slanders; sixth and lastly,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: they have belied a lady; thirdly, they have verified unjust things; and to

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: conclude, they are lying knaves.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: First, I ask thee what they have done; thirdly, I ask thee what’s

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: their offence; sixth and lastly, why they are committed; and, to conclude,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: what you lay to their charge?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Rightly reasoned, and in his own division; and, by my troth,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: there’s one meaning well suited.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Who have you offended, masters, that you are thus bound to

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: your answer? This learned constable is too cunning to be understood.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: What’s your offence?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Sweet Prince, let me go no farther to mine answer: do you hear

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: me, and let this Count kill me. I have deceived even your very eyes: what

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: your wisdoms could not discover, these shallow fools have brought to

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: light; who, in the night overheard me confessing to this man how Don John

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: your brother incensed me to slander the Lady Hero; how you were brought

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: into the orchard and saw me court Margaret in Hero’s garments; how

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: you disgraced her, when you should marry her. My villainy they have upon

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: record; which I had rather seal with my death than repeat over to my

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: shame. The lady is dead upon mine and my master’s false accusation;

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: and, briefly, I desire nothing but the reward of a villain.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Runs not this speech like iron through your blood?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I have drunk poison whiles he utter’d it.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: But did my brother set thee on to this?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Yea; and paid me richly for the practice of it.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: He is compos’d and fram’d of treachery:

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And fled he is upon this villainy.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Sweet Hero! now thy image doth appear

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: In the rare semblance that I lov’d it first.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Come, bring away the plaintiffs: by this time our sexton hath

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: reformed Signior Leonato of the matter. And masters, do not forget to

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: specify, when time and place shall serve, that I am an ass.

lines.speaker: VERGES
lines.text: Here, here comes Master Signior Leonato, and the sexton too.
Re-enter Leonato, Antonio and the Sexton.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Which is the villain? Let me see his eyes,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That, when I note another man like him,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I may avoid him. Which of these is he?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: If you would know your wronger, look on me.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Art thou the slave that with thy breath hast kill’d

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Mine innocent child?

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Yea, even I alone.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No, not so, villain; thou beliest thyself:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Here stand a pair of honourable men;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: A third is fled, that had a hand in it.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I thank you, princes, for my daughter’s death:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Record it with your high and worthy deeds.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: ’Twas bravely done, if you bethink you of it.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I know not how to pray your patience;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yet I must speak. Choose your revenge yourself;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Impose me to what penance your invention

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Can lay upon my sin: yet sinn’d I not

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But in mistaking.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: By my soul, nor I:

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And yet, to satisfy this good old man,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: I would bend under any heavy weight

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: That he’ll enjoin me to.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I cannot bid you bid my daughter live;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That were impossible; but, I pray you both,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Possess the people in Messina here

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: How innocent she died; and if your love

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Can labour aught in sad invention,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Hang her an epitaph upon her tomb,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And sing it to her bones: sing it tonight.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Tomorrow morning come you to my house,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And since you could not be my son-in-law,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Be yet my nephew. My brother hath a daughter,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Almost the copy of my child that’s dead,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And she alone is heir to both of us:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Give her the right you should have given her cousin,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And so dies my revenge.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: O noble sir,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Your over-kindness doth wring tears from me!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I do embrace your offer; and dispose

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: For henceforth of poor Claudio.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Tomorrow then I will expect your coming;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Tonight I take my leave. This naughty man

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Shall face to face be brought to Margaret,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Who, I believe, was pack’d in all this wrong,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Hir’d to it by your brother.

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: No, by my soul she was not;

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: Nor knew not what she did when she spoke to me;

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: But always hath been just and virtuous

lines.speaker: BORACHIO
lines.text: In anything that I do know by her.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Moreover, sir,—which, indeed, is not under white and black,—

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: this plaintiff here, the offender, did call me ass: I beseech you, let it

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: be remembered in his punishment. And also, the watch heard them talk of

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: one Deformed: they say he wears a key in his ear and a lock hanging by it,

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: and borrows money in God’s name, the which he hath used so long and

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: never paid, that now men grow hard-hearted, and will lend nothing for God’s

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: sake. Pray you, examine him upon that point.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: I thank thee for thy care and honest pains.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: Your worship speaks like a most thankful and reverent

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: youth, and I praise God for you.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: There’s for thy pains.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: God save the foundation!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Go, I discharge thee of thy prisoner, and I thank thee.

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: I leave an arrant knave with your worship; which I beseech your

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: worship to correct yourself, for the example of others. God keep your

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: worship! I wish your worship well; God restore you to health! I humbly

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: give you leave to depart, and if a merry meeting may be wished, God

lines.speaker: DOGBERRY
lines.text: prohibit it! Come, neighbour.
[Exeunt Dogberry and Verges.]

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Until tomorrow morning, lords, farewell.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Farewell, my lords: we look for you tomorrow.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: We will not fail.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Tonight I’ll mourn with Hero.
[Exeunt Don Pedro and Claudio.]
[To the Watch.]

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Bring you these fellows on. We’ll talk with

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Margaret,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: How her acquaintance grew with this lewd fellow.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Benedick and Margaret, meeting.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Pray thee, sweet Mistress Margaret, deserve well at my hands by

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: helping me to the speech of Beatrice.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Will you then write me a sonnet in praise of my beauty?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: In so high a style, Margaret, that no man living shall come over

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: it; for, in most comely truth, thou deservest it.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: To have no man come over me! why, shall I always keep below stairs?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Thy wit is as quick as the greyhound’s mouth; it catches.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: And yours as blunt as the fencer’s foils, which hit, but hurt not.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: A most manly wit, Margaret; it will not hurt a woman: and so, I

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: pray thee, call Beatrice. I give thee the bucklers.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Give us the swords, we have bucklers of our own.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: If you use them, Margaret, you must put in the pikes with a

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: vice; and they are dangerous weapons for maids.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Well, I will call Beatrice to you, who I think hath legs.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And therefore will come.
[Exit Margaret.]

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: The god of love,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: That sits above,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And knows me, and knows me,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: How pitiful I deserve,—

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I mean, in singing: but in loving, Leander the good swimmer, Troilus the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: first employer of panders, and a whole book full of these quondam

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: carpet-mongers, whose names yet run smoothly in the even road of a blank

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: verse, why, they were never so truly turned over and over as my poor self

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: in love. Marry, I cannot show it in rime; I have tried: I can find out no

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: rime to ‘lady’ but ‘baby’, an innocent rime; for

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ‘scorn,’ ‘horn’, a hard rime; for ‘school’,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ‘fool’, a babbling rime; very ominous endings: no, I was not

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: born under a riming planet, nor I cannot woo in festival terms.
Enter Beatrice.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Sweet Beatrice, wouldst thou come when I called thee?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Yea, signior; and depart when you bid me.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: O, stay but till then!

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: ‘Then’ is spoken; fare you well now: and yet, ere I

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: go, let me go with that I came for; which is, with knowing what hath

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: passed between you and Claudio.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Only foul words; and thereupon I will kiss thee.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Foul words is but foul wind, and foul wind is but foul breath,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: and foul breath is noisome; therefore I will depart unkissed.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Thou hast frighted the word out of his right sense, so forcible

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: is thy wit. But I must tell thee plainly, Claudio undergoes my challenge,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: and either I must shortly hear from him, or I will subscribe him a coward.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And, I pray thee now, tell me, for which of my bad parts didst thou first

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: fall in love with me?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: For them all together; which maintained so politic a state

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: of evil that they will not admit any good part to intermingle with

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: them. But for which of my good parts did you first suffer love for me?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ‘Suffer love,’ a good epithet! I do suffer love

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: indeed, for I love thee against my will.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: In spite of your heart, I think. Alas, poor heart! If you spite

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: it for my sake, I will spite it for yours; for I will never love that

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: which my friend hates.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Thou and I are too wise to woo peaceably.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: It appears not in this confession: there’s not one wise

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: man among twenty that will praise himself.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: An old, an old instance, Beatrice, that lived in the time of

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: good neighbours. If a man do not erect in this age his own tomb ere he

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: dies, he shall live no longer in monument than the bell rings and the

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: widow weeps.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: And how long is that think you?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Question: why, an hour in clamour and a quarter in rheum:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: therefore is it most expedient for the wise,—if Don Worm, his conscience,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: find no impediment to the contrary,—to be the trumpet of his own virtues,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: as I am to myself. So much for praising myself, who, I myself will bear

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: witness, is praiseworthy. And now tell me, how doth your cousin?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Very ill.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And how do you?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Very ill too.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Serve God, love me, and mend. There will I leave you too, for

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: here comes one in haste.
Enter Ursula.

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Madam, you must come to your uncle. Yonder’s old coil at

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: home: it is proved, my Lady Hero hath been falsely accused, the Prince and

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: Claudio mightily abused; and Don John is the author of all, who is fled

lines.speaker: URSULA
lines.text: and gone. Will you come presently?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Will you go hear this news, signior?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I will live in thy heart, die in thy lap, and be buried in thy

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: eyes; and moreover I will go with thee to thy uncle’s.
[Exeunt.]
Enter Don Pedro, Claudio and Attendants, with music and tapers.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Is this the monument of Leonato?

lines.speaker: A LORD
lines.text: It is, my lord.
[Reads from a scroll.]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Epitaph.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Done to death by slanderous tongues

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Was the Hero that here lies:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Death, in guerdon of her wrongs,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Gives her fame which never dies.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: So the life that died with shame

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Lives in death with glorious fame.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Hang thou there upon the tomb,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Praising her when I am dumb.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Now, music, sound, and sing your solemn hymn.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Song.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Pardon, goddess of the night,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Those that slew thy virgin knight;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: For the which, with songs of woe,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Round about her tomb they go.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Midnight, assist our moan;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Help us to sigh and groan,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Heavily, heavily:

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Graves, yawn and yield your dead,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Till death be uttered,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Heavily, heavily.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Now, unto thy bones good night!

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Yearly will I do this rite.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Good morrow, masters: put your torches out.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: The wolves have prey’d; and look, the gentle day,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Before the wheels of Phoebus, round about

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Dapples the drowsy East with spots of grey.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Thanks to you all, and leave us: fare you well.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Good morrow, masters: each his several way.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Come, let us hence, and put on other weeds;

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: And then to Leonato’s we will go.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And Hymen now with luckier issue speed’s,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Than this for whom we rend’red up this woe!
[Exeunt.]
Enter Leonato, Antonio, Benedick, Beatrice, Margaret, Ursula, Friar Francis and Hero.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Did I not tell you she was innocent?

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: So are the Prince and Claudio, who accus’d her

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Upon the error that you heard debated:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: But Margaret was in some fault for this,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Although against her will, as it appears

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: In the true course of all the question.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Well, I am glad that all things sort so well.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And so am I, being else by faith enforc’d

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: To call young Claudio to a reckoning for it.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Well, daughter, and you gentlewomen all,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Withdraw into a chamber by yourselves,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And when I send for you, come hither mask’d:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The Prince and Claudio promis’d by this hour

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: To visit me.
[Exeunt Ladies.]

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: You know your office, brother;

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: You must be father to your brother’s daughter,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: And give her to young Claudio.

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: Which I will do with confirm’d countenance.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Friar, I must entreat your pains, I think.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: To do what, signior?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: To bind me, or undo me; one of them.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Signior Leonato, truth it is, good signior,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Your niece regards me with an eye of favour.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: That eye my daughter lent her. ’Tis most true.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And I do with an eye of love requite her.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: The sight whereof I think, you had from me,

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: From Claudio, and the Prince. But what’s your will?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Your answer, sir, is enigmatical:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: But, for my will, my will is your good will

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: May stand with ours, this day to be conjoin’d

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: In the state of honourable marriage:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: In which, good friar, I shall desire your help.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: My heart is with your liking.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And my help. Here comes the Prince and Claudio.
Enter Don Pedro and Claudio, with Attendants.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Good morrow to this fair assembly.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Good morrow, Prince; good morrow, Claudio:

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: We here attend you. Are you yet determin’d

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Today to marry with my brother’s daughter?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I’ll hold my mind, were she an Ethiope.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Call her forth, brother: here’s the friar ready.
[Exit Antonio.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: Good morrow, Benedick. Why, what’s the matter,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: That you have such a February face,

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: So full of frost, of storm and cloudiness?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I think he thinks upon the savage bull.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Tush! fear not, man, we’ll tip thy horns with gold,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And all Europa shall rejoice at thee,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: As once Europa did at lusty Jove,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: When he would play the noble beast in love.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Bull Jove, sir, had an amiable low:

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And some such strange bull leap’d your father’s cow,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: And got a calf in that same noble feat,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Much like to you, for you have just his bleat.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: For this I owe you: here comes other reckonings.
Re-enter Antonio, with the ladies masked.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Which is the lady I must seize upon?

lines.speaker: ANTONIO
lines.text: This same is she, and I do give you her.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Why then, she’s mine. Sweet, let me see your face.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: No, that you shall not, till you take her hand

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Before this friar, and swear to marry her.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Give me your hand: before this holy friar,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I am your husband, if you like of me.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And when I liv’d, I was your other wife:
[Unmasking.]

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And when you lov’d, you were my other husband.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Another Hero!

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Nothing certainer:

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: One Hero died defil’d, but I do live,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And surely as I live, I am a maid.

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: The former Hero! Hero that is dead!

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: She died, my lord, but whiles her slander liv’d.

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: All this amazement can I qualify:

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: When after that the holy rites are ended,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: I’ll tell you largely of fair Hero’s death:

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: Meantime, let wonder seem familiar,

lines.speaker: FRIAR
lines.text: And to the chapel let us presently.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Soft and fair, friar. Which is Beatrice?
[Unmasking.]

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I answer to that name. What is your will?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Do not you love me?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Why, no; no more than reason.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Why, then, your uncle and the Prince and Claudio

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Have been deceived; for they swore you did.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Do not you love me?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Troth, no; no more than reason.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Why, then my cousin, Margaret, and Ursula,

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: Are much deceiv’d; for they did swear you did.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: They swore that you were almost sick for me.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: They swore that you were well-nigh dead for me.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: ’Tis no such matter. Then you do not love me?

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: No, truly, but in friendly recompense.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: Come, cousin, I am sure you love the gentleman.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And I’ll be sworn upon ’t that he loves her;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: For here’s a paper written in his hand,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: A halting sonnet of his own pure brain,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Fashion’d to Beatrice.

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: And here’s another,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Writ in my cousin’s hand, stolen from her pocket,

lines.speaker: HERO
lines.text: Containing her affection unto Benedick.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: A miracle! here’s our own hands against our hearts. Come,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I will have thee; but, by this light, I take thee for pity.

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: I would not deny you; but, by this good day, I yield upon great

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: persuasion, and partly to save your life, for I was told you were in a

lines.speaker: BEATRICE
lines.text: consumption.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Peace! I will stop your mouth.
[Kisses her.]

lines.speaker: DON PEDRO
lines.text: How dost thou, Benedick, the married man?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: I’ll tell thee what, Prince; a college of witcrackers cannot flout me

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: out of my humour. Dost thou think I care for a satire or an epigram?

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: No; if man will be beaten with brains, a’ shall wear nothing handsome

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: about him. In brief, since I do purpose to marry, I will think nothing

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: to any purpose that the world can say against it; and therefore never

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: flout at me for what I have said against it, for man is a giddy thing,

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: and this is my conclusion. For thy part, Claudio, I did think to have

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: beaten thee; but, in that thou art like to be my kinsman, live

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: unbruised, and love my cousin.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I had well hoped thou wouldst have denied Beatrice, that I might

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: have cudgelled thee out of thy single life, to make thee a double-dealer;

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: which, out of question, thou wilt be, if my cousin do not look exceeding

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: narrowly to thee.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Come, come, we are friends. Let’s have a dance ere we are

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: married, that we may lighten our own hearts and our wives’ heels.

lines.speaker: LEONATO
lines.text: We’ll have dancing afterward.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: First, of my word; therefore play, music! Prince, thou art sad;

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: get thee a wife, get thee a wife: there is no staff more reverent than one

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: tipped with horn.
Enter Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, your brother John is ta’en in flight,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And brought with armed men back to Messina.

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: Think not on him till tomorrow: I’ll devise thee

lines.speaker: BENEDICK
lines.text: brave punishments for him. Strike up, pipers!
[Dance. Exeunt.]
